get.description:
Returns all card subscriptions under the account, ordered by `createdAt` descending (most recently created first).

The `subaccountId`, `cardId`, `bankAccountId`, `state`, `networkBulkFeedId`, `companyId`, `legalEntityId` and `legalEntityName` filters are independent and combine additively; supplying more than one narrows the result set to subscriptions matching **all** of them.

`companyId`, `legalEntityId` and `legalEntityName` filter on the card's cardholder as it is now: `corporate.id`, `corporate.legalEntity.id` and `corporate.legalEntity.name` (see the [Glossary](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/glossary)). Each is an exact match; `legalEntityName` is case-sensitive, and each of `legalEntityId` and `legalEntityName` never matches a cardholder whose legal entity lacks that field, so copy it from the cardholder (`expand=cardholder` shows each cardholder's company and legal entity in the same response). For example, this returns the active subscriptions of one legal entity on one feed:

`GET /card-subscriptions?networkBulkFeedId=<feed>&legalEntityId=<id>&state=active`

These three filters read cardholder data, so they need the `cardholder:read` scope, like `expand=cardholder`. Without it the request returns `403`.

Filtering by `state` accepts any of the states a card subscription reports in its response payload:

- `pending`: enrolled from a network roster while the card is still inactive at the network. The subscription is fully enrolled and billable, but has not yet transacted.
- `active`: also returns subscriptions still completing activation, which already report their own `state` as `active`.
- `deactivated`, `expired`, `reqSCA`, `failed-to-create`: matched exactly.

This endpoint supports [offset-based pagination](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/pagination). Pagination links preserve any filters applied to the original request.

Use `expand` to embed each subscription's card and cardholder in the same response (`?expand=card,cardholder`) instead of calling `GET /cards/{cardId}` and `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` per item. Each embedded resource appears under the item's `_embedded` with the exact body its own endpoint serves, and requires that endpoint's scope (`cards:read` for `card`, `cardholder:read` for `cardholder`). Pagination links preserve `expand` like any other parameter.

Returns detailed information about a specific card subscription by its identifier, including its data-sharing state.

Add `expand=card,cardholder` to embed the card and cardholder under `_embedded` in the same response instead of fetching them separately. Each embedded resource is the exact body its own endpoint serves and requires that endpoint's scope (`cards:read` for `card`, `cardholder:read` for `cardholder`).

patch.description:
Updates an existing card subscription, allowing changes to its data-sharing state. Subscriptions that were enrolled in bulk, and where `enrollmentType = 'network-bulk'` cannot be updated.

**Note:** setting a card subscription to a `deactivated` state is a final action that cannot be undone.

If the card also has a linked bank account, deactivating it stops that bank account's feed for the card too; to stop only the card network data, ask your Astrada contact.

When deactivating, you can send an optional `deactivationReason` to record why the card was deactivated.

delete.description:
Works in the sandbox only (`https://api.sandbox.astrada.co`), for
clearing test data between runs. Production has no delete call: there
you deactivate card subscriptions with `PATCH`.

Deletes a card subscription and the data it owns, and cannot be undone.
When it is the last subscription on its card, the card, cardholder,
stored token and transactions are removed as well.

The call returns when the delete has finished: `204` when it is done,
`502` when a step failed. Retrying a failed delete is always safe:
completed steps are skipped on replay.

post.summary: Unlock a card's verification attempt lockout
post.description:
Clear the cross-network verification **attempt lockout** for a card,
identified by its `cardId`. This re-enables verification attempts for the
card after it has been throttled by too many recent hard failures; the
account-scoped, cross-network throttle that protects the non-HIGHEST tiers
(Visa/Stripe, Mastercard/TNS). Idempotent: unlocking a card that has no
active lock succeeds and clears nothing. The HIGHEST per-fingerprint lockout
is **not** affected by this endpoint.

200.description:
The card's attempt lockout was cleared, or the card had no active lock
(idempotent).

get.description:
Returns a list of all cards linked to the account.

By default, `GET /cards` returns cards ordered by the latest updatedAt. You can combine the different filters as documented.

Use `networkBulkFeedId` to filter the list to cards enrolled through a given network bulk feed. An unknown feed id returns an empty page. It combines with `expand=cardholder`.

Use `expand=cardholder` to embed each card's cardholder under `_embedded` in the same response instead of calling `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` per item. The embedded body is the exact body that endpoint serves and requires its `cardholder:read` scope. Pagination links preserve `expand` like any other parameter.

This endpoint supports [offset-based pagination](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/pagination).

Returns detailed information about a specific card by its identifier.

Add `expand=cardholder` to embed the cardholder under `_embedded` in the same response instead
of calling `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` separately. The embedded body is the exact body that
endpoint serves and requires its `cardholder:read` scope.

Returns the card's current cardholder information. Answers `404` when the card has no cardholder.

For the company and legal entity the card belonged to at the time of a given transaction, use
`expand=cardholder` on that transaction instead: `GET /transactions/{transactionId}?expand=cardholder`.

patch.description:
Updates cardholder information for a specific card. Use this endpoint to simulate cardholder data that would typically be received through a Network Bulk Feed. This is useful for testing your integration against bulk-enrolled cards without waiting for actual network feed data.

**Note:** This endpoint requires the `cardholder:write` scope and must be directly enabled by Astrada.

post.summary: List the available enrollment methods given a card BIN
post.description:
List the available enrollment methods given a card BIN.

The Unified Enrollment SDK v2 calls this endpoint for each card: when a person presses **Continue** on the card number screen, with the first 8 to 11 digits they typed (8 by default), and on an employee page that opens on the card form, once 8 digits are typed there. It sends the session's `subaccountId` with the digits, and asks again with the digits alone when that answers `400` or `403`. It routes the session from the answer together with `GET /bin-lookup`. The SDK token therefore needs `enrollment-methods:write`. If your own backend calls it, send up to 11 digits for the most precise answer.

Send `subaccountId` to ask whether that subaccount can enroll this card one at a time with `POST /card-subscriptions`. The response then adds `singleDecision`, from the single-enrollment controls that create runs for the subaccount, and `singleEligible` and `availableEnrollmentMethods` follow it. Create also checks the `country` sent with the card; this request has no country, so `singleDecision` does not cover that check. Without `subaccountId`, the response is about the card alone and no subaccount is read.

When Mastercard's live card data is temporarily unavailable, the response falls back to Astrada's stored card data instead of failing, and `binInfo` comes from that stored data. `bulkLikelihood` is then capped at `medium`, except for BINs with proven bulk history, which stay `proven`, so `network-bulk` is then offered only for those proven BINs. When nothing decides the grade, `bulkLikelihood` is omitted and `unavailable` lists it; `singleEligible` is then `true` and `availableEnrollmentMethods` is `["cardholder-single"]`, unless `singleDecision` refuses the card. Retry later for a full answer.

400.description: The request failed validation, for example a `bin` that is not 6 to 11 digits or a `subaccountId` that is not a UUID. A `subaccountId` that is not one of your account's subaccounts also gets `400`, with the detail `Given subaccount is not valid`.

post.description:
Creates an enrollment link for one of your subaccounts. The link opens a page on
Astrada's SDK host where the person who has it enrolls their own cards into that
subaccount.

- A personal link (`kind: cardholder`) is for one employee. It allows up to 5 session
  starts and is used up by the first session that completes something.
- A team link (`kind: team`) is for sharing. Each session start counts as a use, up to
  `maxUses`.

The response's `url` carries the link's secret after `#`. This response is the only
one that returns it, and it is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Astrada stores only
a hash of the secret. In sandbox the `url` starts with
`https://sdk.sandbox.astrada.co/unified/v2/enroll.html#`.

Requires `subaccounts:write`.

Refusals carry a `code`:

- `404` `SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: `subaccountId` is not one of your subaccounts.
- `409` `ENROLLMENT_LINKS_NOT_ENABLED`: enrollment links are not enabled for your
  account.
- `409` `CARD_ENROLLMENT_OFF`: card enrollment is off for the subaccount (its
  `enrollmentPolicy.cardEnrollment` is `false`). The hosted page offers card enrollment
  only, so a link would have nothing to enroll. This check runs before the daily limit
  is counted, so a refused request does not use it up.
- `400` `LINK_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED`: `organizationName` or `platformName` is a
  well-known brand name, such as a card network or a large bank, matched ignoring case,
  accents and punctuation. Astrada and Plaid are also refused inside a longer name.
- `429` `RATE_LIMITED`: your account has created 2,000 links today (UTC), team links
  made with `POST /subaccounts/{subaccountId}/team-link` included.

A link made before card enrollment was turned off starts no session while card
enrollment stays off: `POST /enrollment-link-sessions/preview` and
`POST /enrollment-link-sessions` answer `409` `CARD_ENROLLMENT_OFF`, and no start is
counted.

400.description:
The body failed validation, and `errors` names the field. Or `organizationName` or
`platformName` is a well-known brand name, with `code` `LINK_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED`.

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: That platform name is not allowed.

get.description:
Lists the enrollment links of one of your subaccounts, newest first, without their
`url`.

A page holds at most `limit` links and can hold fewer, even none, while more remain.
Keep following `_links.next` until a response has no `_links.next`. Use its `href` as
it is: it keeps your `subaccountId`, `state` and `limit`.

A subaccount that has no links, or that is not one of yours, gives an empty list.

Requires `subaccounts:write`, so link details such as references and counts never
reach a browser SDK token.

parameters.description: The subaccount whose links to list.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only links in this state. `active` and `expired` are told apart by `expiresAt`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most links a page holds.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Where the page starts, as set in `_links.next`. A cursor from another subaccount's
listing, or one that does not decode, answers `400` `INVALID_CURSOR`.

A query parameter is not valid, and `errors` names it. Or the cursor is not one this
listing gave out, with `code` `INVALID_CURSOR`.

get.description:
Returns one of your enrollment links with its sessions, oldest first, without its
`url`. With the `cardsubscription` webhooks, this is how you see what happened on the
hosted page.

Each session's `outcome` holds the ids the hosted page reported. Nothing checks them
against the card or bank APIs: the `cardsubscription` webhooks are the source of truth
for what was enrolled.

Requires `subaccounts:write`. A link that is not one of yours answers `404` with
`code` `ENROLLMENT_LINK_NOT_FOUND`. A link and its sessions are kept for 90 days after
`expiresAt`, then answer `404`.

post.description:
Revokes one of your enrollment links. No body. An active link, an expired one
included, becomes `revoked`: no session starts from it again, and its open sessions
fail their next token refresh, so their access ends within one access token lifetime
(at most 300 seconds). A link that is already used or revoked is returned as it is.

Requires `subaccounts:write`. A link that is not one of yours answers `404` with
`code` `ENROLLMENT_LINK_NOT_FOUND`.

post.description:
Starts a bulk enrollment kickoff for a whole card program. The request records the
company, the card program admin, an optional bank contact and program size, and the
admin's consent, and Astrada's onboarding team takes it from there with the issuing
bank. The Unified Enrollment SDK calls this endpoint when an admin sends the bulk
kickoff form (in SDK v1, with `bulkFlow: "kickoff"`); you can also call it directly.

Nothing is enrolled yet at this point. Once the bank has issued the network
reference, register the feed with `POST /network-bulk-feeds` and pass this
enrollment's `id` as `networkBulkEnrollmentId`; the enrollment then moves to
`feed-created` and links to the feed.

The subaccount must belong to the calling account. The BIN's bulk eligibility is not
re-checked here. A validation failure or an unknown subaccount answers `400`.

A program has one open kickoff at a time. A program is the calling account, the
`subaccountId`, the `network` and the first 8 digits of the `bin`; a `bin` shorter than
8 digits matches only a kickoff with exactly the same digits. A kickoff is open while it
is `requested` and was created less than 90 days ago, or while it is `feed-created` and
its feed is live (not `failed` or `deactivated`, and not deleted), at any age. When the
program already has an open kickoff that another request wrote, this request stores no
second kickoff and answers `200` with that kickoff's summary (`alreadyOpen: true`),
whatever new `requestId` it sent, or none. Astrada keeps the card admin named in this
request with the open kickoff, so its onboarding team knows who else is waiting, and the
open kickoff stays the only one they work on. A repeat of the same `requestId` is kept once.
`GET /network-bulk-enrollments/open` answers the same question before the form.
Two kickoffs for one program sent at the same time store one kickoff between them.

The 90 days count from the kickoff's `createdAt`. Once a `requested` kickoff is 90 days
old it stops holding its program: nothing is written to it, it keeps its state and can
still be read, and the next kickoff for the program is created with `201`. A `cancelled`
kickoff, or one whose feed failed, was deactivated or was deleted, does not hold its
program either.

Requires the `network-bulk-enrollments:write` scope. Tokens that only hold
`network-bulk-feeds:write` are still accepted, so existing integrations keep working.

200.description:
A stored kickoff, returned unchanged, in one of two shapes:

- An enrollment with this `requestId` already exists: the full enrollment, as your
  request wrote it.
- The program already has an open kickoff that another request wrote: its summary,
  marked `alreadyOpen: true`, with the `requestId` this request sent (`null` when it
  sent none) and only the `self` link. Names, emails, bank contact, `binInfo`, consent
  and outreach are left out.

201.description: Resource created. The program had no open kickoff, so this request wrote one.

get.summary: Check for an open network bulk enrollment
get.description:
Answers whether a card program already has an open bulk enrollment kickoff, before anyone
fills in the kickoff form. The Unified Enrollment SDK calls it while it looks up a card, and
shows "Already under way" instead of the program screen when the program has one; you can
also call it directly.

A program is the calling account, the `subaccountId`, the `network` and the card's first 8
digits (`bin`). The rule is the one `POST /network-bulk-enrollments` uses: a kickoff is open
while it is `requested` and was created less than 90 days ago, or while it is `feed-created`
and its feed is live, at any age. The account comes from the token, never from the query.

The answer carries only the open kickoff's `enrollmentId`, `state` and `requestedAt`. A
`bin` of more or fewer than 8 digits, a missing or unknown parameter, or an `accountId` in
the query answers `400`.

Requires the `network-bulk-enrollments:write` scope, the one the kickoff itself takes.
Tokens that only hold `network-bulk-feeds:write` are also accepted. A token with only a read
scope answers `403`.

parameters.name: subaccountId
parameters.description: The subaccount of the card program. Must belong to the calling account to find anything.

200.description: Whether the program has an open kickoff.

get.description:
Returns a network bulk enrollment by its identifier. Once a feed has been registered
with this enrollment's id on `POST /network-bulk-feeds`, the representation carries
`networkBulkFeedId` and a `networkBulkFeed` link. An enrollment that belongs to
another account answers `404`.

Requires the `network-bulk-enrollments:read` scope. Tokens that only hold
`network-bulk-feeds:read` are still accepted, so existing integrations keep working.

post.description:
Asks Astrada to confirm that a card program can join a network bulk feed. Astrada
checks with the issuing bank and the network by hand, then emails the card program
admin with the answer. Unlike `POST /network-bulk-enrollments`, this is not a kickoff:
it does not start outreach to the bank and can never be linked to a feed. A validation
failure or an unknown subaccount answers `400`, as for the kickoff.

A program has one open confirmation request at a time. A program is the calling account,
the `subaccountId`, the `network` and the `bin`. Every stored request is open for 30 days
from its `createdAt`, as nothing closes a request yet. When the program already has an
open request that another request wrote, this request stores nothing and answers `200`
with that request's summary (`alreadyOpen: true`), whatever new `requestId` it sent. No
second request reaches Astrada. Two requests for one program sent at the same time store
one request between them.

Once a request is 30 days old it stops holding its program: nothing is written to it, and
the next request for the program is stored with `201` and reaches Astrada again.

The route answers these errors as `application/problem+json`, with `title` and `detail`:

| Status | When | `detail` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The body does not pass validation. `errors` lists each field that failed. | `Request parameters are invalid` |
| `400` | `subaccountId` is not a subaccount of the calling account. | `The subaccount {subaccountId} was not found` |
| `403` | The token holds neither `network-bulk-enrollments:write` nor `network-bulk-feeds:write`. | `You do not have permission to access the requested resource` |
| `500` | The request could not be completed. | `An unexpected error occurred` or `The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request` |

200.description:
A stored confirmation request, returned unchanged, in one of two shapes:

- A confirmation with this `requestId` already exists: the full confirmation, as your
  request wrote it.
- The program already has an open request that another request wrote: its summary,
  marked `alreadyOpen: true`, with the `requestId` this request sent. Names, emails,
  bank contact, `binInfo` and `grade` are left out.

Both are plain JSON with no `_links`.

201.description: Resource created. The program had no open request, so this request wrote one. Served as plain JSON rather than HAL, since a confirmation has no GET and so carries no `_links`.

get.description:
Returns detailed information about a specific subaccount by its identifier, including configuration details and associated data.

`_links.team-link` appears when enrollment links are enabled for the account, the token holds `card-subscriptions:write` or `subaccounts:write`, and the subaccount's card enrollment is on (its `enrollmentPolicy.cardEnrollment` is not `false`). It points to `POST /subaccounts/{subaccountId}/team-link`, which creates a team link for the subaccount. An enrollment link session's token never gets it.

200.description: Details of the subaccount giving the accountId and subaccountId

patch.description:
Update a subaccount name and configurations.
All updated configurations are validated against the capabilities of the main account to ensure compliance.
It is possible to add new networks and/or regions but it is not possible to remove any configurations that were previously set.
`configurations` replaces the whole object: send every network the subaccount has (a network left out is refused with `Delete a configuration is not supported.`), and every block list you want to keep (a block list left out goes back to the account's default).

Each network's `countries` can be set to either an array of specific ISO 3166 alpha-3 country codes, or the string `"*"` to inherit all countries from the parent account's capabilities for that network.

When using `"*"`, the subaccount will automatically reflect the parent account's current country list. If the parent account's capabilities change, subaccounts configured with `"*"` will inherit the updated countries.

The single and bulk enrollment configurations are optional. Countries are set per network: each one's country list is the network's `countries`, limited to the countries the account allows for that way of enrolling. The supported card types for single and bulk enrollment is CONSUMER, while the supported funding card types is DEBIT. If not provided, the block rules for both card types will default to the parent account's default block rule for that network and enrollment level. A list you send is combined with the account's defaults, so it can add blocks but never remove one of the account's defaults. Visa consumer debit and prepaid cards are blocked at the network level regardless of these settings; see `networkBlockedCards` on the subaccount.

To set the default rule on the parent account, please reach out to your account manager or support.

200.description:
Specified subaccount updated successfully. The body is the same effective read
model `GET /subaccounts/{subaccountId}` returns (`enrollmentPolicy`,
`bankLinkingPolicy`, `plaidEndCustomer` and `enforceIssuerCountry` resolved
against the parent account, and `networkBlockedCards` resolved from the platform
network configuration), so it may include account-level and platform-level
settings that were not part of the request and that the subaccount stores no
value for.

When the request's `enrollmentPolicy` holds keys this endpoint does not accept, the
body also carries `ignoredFields`, which names each of them. Unknown keys outside
`enrollmentPolicy` are ignored and not listed.

post.description:
Creates a team link for the subaccount: the route for the SDK's "Invite your team"
ending, which calls it with the SDK token's `card-subscriptions:write`. An API client
may call it with `subaccounts:write`. No body.

`_links.team-link` on `GET /subaccounts/{subaccountId}` points here when the route is
available to the caller.

The link has the team defaults: it expires after 14 days and allows 50 session starts.
The response holds only what the SDK screen shows, and is sent with
`Cache-Control: no-store`. Every call makes a new link. A new link does not revoke an
older one: each link ends at its own expiry, when its session starts are used up, or
when it is revoked. Revoke a link you no longer want shared with
`POST /enrollment-links/{linkId}/revoke`.

Refusals carry a `code`:

- `403` `LINK_SESSION_FORBIDDEN`: the token is an enrollment link session's. It holds
  `card-subscriptions:write` too, but cannot make links.
- `404` `SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: the subaccount is not one of your account's.
- `409` `ENROLLMENT_LINKS_NOT_ENABLED`: enrollment links are not enabled for your
  account.
- `409` `CARD_ENROLLMENT_OFF`: card enrollment is off for the subaccount (its
  `enrollmentPolicy.cardEnrollment` is `false`). The hosted page offers card enrollment
  only, so a link would have nothing to enroll. This check runs before the daily limits
  are counted, so a refused request does not use them up.
- `429` `RATE_LIMITED`: 20 links were made here for the subaccount today (UTC), or your
  account has created 2,000 links today.

A link made before card enrollment was turned off starts no session while card
enrollment stays off: `POST /enrollment-link-sessions/preview` and
`POST /enrollment-link-sessions` answer `409` `CARD_ENROLLMENT_OFF`, and no start is
counted.

get.description:
Returns a list of all subaccounts associated with the account.

This endpoint supports [cursor-based pagination](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/pagination).

post.description:
Creates a new subaccount, allowing you to set network and regional configurations.

Each network's `countries` can be set to either an array of specific ISO 3166 alpha-3 country codes, or the string `"*"` to inherit all countries from the parent account's capabilities for that network.

When using `"*"`, the subaccount will automatically reflect the parent account's current country list. If the parent account's capabilities change, subaccounts configured with `"*"` will inherit the updated countries.

The single and bulk enrollment configurations are optional. Countries are set per network: each one's country list is the network's `countries`, limited to the countries the account allows for that way of enrolling.
The supported card types for single and bulk enrollment is CONSUMER, while the supported funding card types is DEBIT. If not provided, the block rules for both card types will default to the parent account's default block rule for that network and enrollment level. A list you send is combined with the account's defaults, so it can add blocks but never remove one of the account's defaults. Visa consumer debit and prepaid cards are blocked at the network level regardless of these settings; see `networkBlockedCards` on the subaccount.

To set the default rule on the parent account, please reach out to your account manager or support.

against the parent account, and `networkBlockedCards` resolved from the platform
network configuration), not the raw create-time snapshot. Account-level and
platform-level settings therefore appear here even though the new subaccount
stores no value for them.

get.description:
Returns a list of all transactions under the account.

By default, `GET /transactions` returns transactions ordered by the latest `createdAt`. You can combine the different filters as documented.

This endpoint supports [cursor-based pagination](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/pagination).

Add `expand` to embed each transaction's related resources under `_embedded` in the same response,
for example `expand=cardSubscription,card,cardholder`. Each embedded resource is the exact body its own
endpoint serves, shows its current values (not those at the time of the transaction) except
`cardholder.corporate`, which is resolved as of the transaction's date (see the `expand` parameter), and
requires that endpoint's scope: `card-subscriptions:read` for `cardSubscription`, `cards:read` for `card`,
`cardholder:read` for `cardholder`. Transactions without a given related resource simply omit that key.
Pagination links preserve `expand`.

For the company and legal entity a card belonged to when the transaction happened, use `expand=cardholder`
and read `cardholder.corporate.id` and `cardholder.corporate.legalEntity`. They are the values in effect on
the transaction's `transactionOccurrenceDate` (through the end of that UTC day), or at the transaction's
`createdAt` when that is null, so a card that later moved to another company or legal entity keeps its
historical attribution on past transactions.
Transactions themselves do not carry a company identifier.

To list the transactions of one company or legal entity, filter with `companyId`, `legalEntityId` or
`legalEntityName`. They match the cardholder's `corporate.id`, `corporate.legalEntity.id` and
`corporate.legalEntity.name` on the transaction date: the values `expand=cardholder` returns on each
transaction, not the cardholder's current ones (see the [Glossary](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/glossary)).
Each is an exact, case-sensitive match, so copy the value from a transaction's `expand=cardholder`.
The filters use the same as-of resolution as `expand=cardholder`, including the earliest recorded values
for a transaction dated before Astrada started recording the card's corporate history. A transaction
whose card has no cardholder data, or whose card `GET /cards/{cardId}` no longer returns, does not match, just
as `expand` embeds no `cardholder` for it.
They combine with each other and with `transactionMessageId`, `cardId`, `subaccountId` and
`networkBulkFeedId`: supplying more than one returns only the transactions matching **all** of them.
The one exception: `cardId` and `networkBulkFeedId` cannot be sent together, and the request answers `400`.
Transactions without a card never match. For example, this returns one legal entity's transactions on
one feed:

`GET /transactions?networkBulkFeedId=<feed>&legalEntityId=<id>`

URL-encode the values. In `legalEntityName` a space is `%20` (or `+`), and a literal `+` is read as a
space, so send a `+` in the name as `%2B`. Send each filter once. Leading and trailing spaces are
ignored. A value that is empty or only spaces, or longer than 255 characters, is refused with `400`.

With any of these filters a page can hold fewer than `limit` transactions, even none, while
`_links.next` is present. Keep following `_links.next` until it is absent.

These three filters read cardholder data, so they need the `cardholder:read` scope, like
`expand=cardholder`. Without it the request returns `403`.

Returns a transaction by its unique identifier, including details about the transaction's state and relevant transactional data.

`expand=cardSubscription,card,cardholder`. Each embedded resource is the exact body its own endpoint

the transaction's `transactionOccurrenceDate` (through the end of that UTC day), or at the transaction's

Return a transaction message by its unique identifier, including details about the transaction's type and relevant transactional data.

Transaction messages are also delivered embedded in the transaction payload: `transaction.created` and `transaction.updated` webhook payloads include a projection of every correlated message under `_embedded.messages[]`, each entry carrying its financial fields plus a per-message `superseded` marker. See [Event Types](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/event-types) for the full payload structure.
Return a raw transaction message by the transaction message unique identifier.

get.description:
Returns detailed information about a specific bank link by its identifier.

If the bank link is in `pending` state and the hosted link URL has expired, this endpoint will automatically refresh the URL and return the updated link.

Once the user has finished the hosted flow, a read of the link answers `completed`: the link completes without a `PATCH` from you.

patch.description:
Completes a bank link enrollment, transitioning it from `pending` to `completed` state. The request body must contain `state: "completed"`.

When a bank link is completed, the system exchanges the enrollment credentials with the provider, creates a bank subscription (connection), and discovers the associated bank accounts.

A link that is no longer `pending` answers `409`; read it with `GET /bank-links/{bankLinkId}`.

The PATCH response echoes the bank link record only. The discovered `bankAccounts` (with each account's `cardIds` and any minted `cards`) are returned by `GET /bank-links/{bankLinkId}`, not by this PATCH.

delete.description:
Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Deletes a bank link and all associated resources, including the bank subscription, bank accounts, and bank transactions.

Cards are not deleted. A `bank-feed` subscription created at completion is deactivated; a card enrolled by its number only loses its bank account. Each still-active account sends `bankaccount.state_changed`, and each changed subscription sends `cardsubscription.updated`.

**Note:** This action is irreversible and will revoke access to the connected financial institution.

post.description:
Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Triggers a manual sync of transactions for the bank link's associated subscription. This fetches the latest transactions from the financial institution.

Transaction syncs also occur automatically via provider webhooks and scheduled jobs. Use this endpoint to force an immediate sync when needed.

While another sync of the same connection is running, this call answers `200` and syncs nothing; send it again shortly. When the bank is temporarily unavailable it answers `503`.

get.description: Returns detailed information about a specific bank account by its identifier.

patch.description:
Updates a bank account. Card links are detected automatically: a scheduled sweep re-checks each cardless credit account every few hours and links an enrolled card whose last 4 digits match the account's mask, without any API call. This endpoint is the manual override: use it to pre-link a card immediately, correct an assignment, or import history.

Each card in `cardIds` must belong to the same subaccount as the bank account. A card can only be linked to one bank account at a time; attempting to link a card that is already associated with another bank account will return a `409 Conflict` error.

A card that cannot take a bank-account link is also rejected with `409 Conflict` before any change is applied: one whose only enrollment is a bulk feed, or whose subscriptions are all in a dead, non-attachable state. The `message` names the card and says whether it is bulk-enrolled or has no live subscription. This body, like the "already linked" `409`, has no `code`. If the cards directory cannot be consulted, this screen is skipped (fail-open) rather than blocking the update.

`cardIds` is a full replacement. Send `cardIds: []` to clear explicit links (the scheduled mask sweep can re-link a matching card on its next run).

Cards Astrada created for the individual cardholders of a pooled American Express billing account are managed by the platform: a `cardIds` list without them does not remove them (they leave when the card is deactivated or the account is disconnected or deleted). An enrolled card that was linked for one such cardholder can be removed here, and stays removed: it is not linked again automatically.

Optionally include a `backfill` object with `startDate` and/or `endDate` to trigger a backfill of historical bank transactions for the specified date range. An automatically detected link re-matches the account's already-synced unmatched transactions around the new card's activity on its own; IMPORTING bank history from before the link (pulling older transactions from the provider) still happens only through this endpoint's `backfill`.

The current card set is always readable at `GET /bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}` (`cardIds`), and `GET /bank-accounts?cardId=` finds the account a card is linked to.

delete.description:
Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Deletes a bank account and all associated bank transactions, transaction matches, and card links.

Cards are not deleted. A `bank-feed` subscription created from this account is deactivated; a card enrolled by its number only loses its bank account. The account sends `bankaccount.state_changed` with reason `deleted`.

**Note:** This action is irreversible. Deleting the last account of a bank connection also removes the connection at the bank.

post.description:
Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Imports historical bank transactions for this account from the provider over a date range, then runs matching against the account's full current card set. Unlike the `backfill` object on `PATCH /bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}` (which imports history for cards being added in that same request), this endpoint recovers a date window without touching card links. Each imported bank transaction sends `banktransaction.created` and each new match `transaction.match.created`.

Requires a backing connection. Starting a backfill while another sync already holds the account's connection returns `409 Conflict`; retry shortly.

For Mastercard accounts at US banks (`provider: mastercard`, `countryCode: USA`), `loadHistoric: true` additionally asks the provider to generate deep history (up to 2 years) for this account before the import runs. This is a billable provider operation and generation is asynchronous on the provider side: if the immediate import returns few rows, re-run the same window without the flag once generation completes (typically within minutes). Providers without a deep-history operation reject the flag with `400 Bad Request`.

requestBody.description: Date range to import. Both bounds are optional; send an empty object for the default window.

post.description: Creates a new hosted link URL for the user to re-authenticate an account in `auth_required`. Any other state answers `400`. To ask the bank for new transactions, use `POST /bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}/transactions/refresh`.

Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Asks the data provider to check this account's institution **now**, instead of waiting for its own schedule (typically one to four checks a day). The call returns once the check has run, usually within seconds but occasionally 30 seconds or more. It imports nothing itself: anything the check finds arrives through the normal update path within moments.

**Billable per successful call.** Use it at moments that matter, not on a timer. Returns `400 Bad Request` when the account has no backing connection, or when its provider or institution doesn't support an on-demand refresh (e.g. some card issuers), and `502 Bad Gateway` when the provider's check fails.

202.description: The provider has run its check of the institution. `durationMs` is how long that check took, not an import; any changes it found arrive through the normal update path.

Returns a list of transaction matches for a subaccount. Each match represents a link between a bank transaction and a card transaction, along with a confidence score and the reasoning behind the match.

By default, matches are filtered to `MEDIUM` confidence and above. Use the `minConfidence` parameter to adjust the threshold.

get.description: Returns detailed information about a specific transaction match, including the confidence level, numeric score, and a breakdown of the scoring factors.

Retrieve card information such as network, type, and issuing bank by providing the card's
BIN (Bank Identification Number): the first 6 to 11 digits of the card number. Never send
the full card number; more than 11 digits is rejected with `400`.

The card details are found under the first 6 digits. One 6-digit BIN can be shared by
issuers in several countries, so for a Mastercard card looked up with 6 to 11 digits,
Astrada also runs a more precise issuer-country check on the digits sent. That check can
return a different `issuerCountry`, `issuerRegion` and `issuerName` than the first 6
digits alone would. Send more digits (up to 11) for a more precise issuer country; never
send the full card number.

When the digits sent match card ranges in more than one country, the response keeps the
6-digit values and adds `issuerCountryAmbiguous`, `issuerCountryCandidates`, and a
`warnings` entry with code `ISSUER_COUNTRY_NOT_CONFIRMED`. In every other case none of
these three fields is present.

Lookups for every other network are unaffected. If the precise check gives no answer, the
request still succeeds with the 6-digit values. In sandbox the precise check is not run,
so sandbox responses never include these fields.

or from `GET /transactions?transactionMessageId=`.

and `transaction-messages:read`: the transaction and its messages are read
from the public API to carry over the network reference and the current
hold and settled amounts.

`adjustment` and `reversal` are checked against the hold Astrada has
processed so far and rejected with `409` when there is nothing to adjust
or reverse. The check is best effort: a step published immediately after
another may see the earlier state.

post.description:
Creates a new bank link to initiate a bank enrollment. The response includes a `hostedLink` URL where the user can connect their bank account via Plaid.

The hosted link expires after 4 hours. If the link expires before the user completes enrollment, retrieve the bank link via `GET /bank-links/{bankLinkId}` to get a refreshed URL.

Creating a bank link with an ID that already exists for the account will return a `409 Conflict` error, unless the existing link has expired.

A refused create returns a JSON body with `statusCode` and `message`. These errors also carry a `code`, a stable name to branch on so that you never match on `message` text (the `409` above has no `code`):

- `404` `SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: `subaccountId` is not one of the account's subaccounts. Nothing is created. The message is `Subaccount not found for this account`.
- `403` `BANK_ENROLLMENT_DISABLED`: a create is refused when the account has locked bank enrollment (`enrollmentPolicy.bankEnrollmentLocked` is `true` on the subaccount) and the subaccount's `enrollmentPolicy.bankEnrollment` value does not allow a bank link for this card. Otherwise the check does not refuse. Nothing is created. The message is `Bank linking is not enabled for this card on this account`. The body also has a `reason`: `bank-enrollment-off` when the setting is `off`, `network-not-allowed` when it does not allow the card's network, and `network-unknown` when it limits the networks and the request does not show the card's network. The card's network comes from the request: American Express when the link uses the `amex_only` customization, otherwise `bin6` (a first digit of `4` is Visa, `2` or `5` is Mastercard, and any other digit, a `3` included, is unknown). Without `bin6` it is unknown.
- `403` `MASTERCARD_CLIENT_NOT_PROVISIONED` and `PLAID_EC_NOT_PROVISIONED`: the account is not set up for bank linking on that provider yet. The messages are `This account is not set up for Mastercard bank linking yet` and `This account is not set up for Plaid bank linking yet`.
- `403` `PLAID_CUSTOMIZATION_NOT_PROVISIONED`: Plaid refused the Link customization this link asked for, because the account's Plaid client cannot use it, and no fallback applied. Nothing is created. The message is `This account is not fully set up for Plaid bank linking yet`. A customization other than `amex_only` (one set by the bank-linking policy's `plaidLinkCustomizationName`) answers this at once. When Plaid refuses `amex_only`, from `filters.linkCustomizationName` or from the policy, the create is retried once with the environment's pinned customization in its place, or with no customization when the environment pins none. If Plaid accepts the retry, the link is created as usual: its hosted session opens without the `amex_only` customization, and its completion is still held to American Express institutions. For `amex_only`, only a refused retry answers this error. Astrada fixes it in the account's Plaid setup, so sending the same request again does not help.
- `400` `INVALID_LINK_FILTERS`: `filters` asks for more than the account's bank-linking policy allows, or for a customization that is not allowed.
- `400` `PROVIDER_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_ACCOUNT`: `provider` is not enabled for the account.
- `400` `PROVIDER_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_COUNTRY`: no provider supports `countryCode` for the chosen `provider`.
- `503` `BANK_FEED_OWNER_NOT_CONFIGURED`: `persona: cardholder` in an environment where cardholder links are not set up yet. Nothing is created; a link without `persona: cardholder` still works. The message is `Cardholder bank linking is not available yet`.

A body that breaks the field formats (for example an empty `accountTypes` or a lower-case `countryCode`) answers `400` with message `Bad Request` and an `errors` list naming each field, and no `code`.

By default, `GET /bank-accounts` returns bank accounts ordered by the latest `createdAt`.

This endpoint supports cursor-based pagination.

post.summary: Link enrolled cards to bank accounts (admin backfill)
post.description:
Admin backfill/retry for immediate mask-linking: matches the subaccount's ENROLLED cards against its credit bank accounts by mask (an enrolled card's last 4 digits) and links each exact match. The same exactly-one-or-skip rules as completion-time linking apply: a mask matching multiple cards, or multiple accounts claiming a mask, links nothing (the scheduled mask sweep retries this every few hours). Idempotent: already-linked pairs are skipped. Intended for onboarding backfills (cards enrolled before the bank link) and recovery after a transient directory failure at completion. Emits no webhook; linked cardIds appear on subsequent bank-account reads.

The body takes `subaccountId` only; any other field is a `400`. The admin actions (minting cards for cardless accounts, the cardholder backfill) are on `POST /bank-accounts/maintenance` at `banking:admin`.

201.description: Backfill executed. Maps each bank account that gained links to the card ids linked in this run (empty object when nothing matched).

post.summary: Bank account maintenance for a subaccount
post.description:
Needs the `banking:admin` scope. If your API client does not have it, the API answers `403 Forbidden`; ask Astrada to enable it if you need this operation.

Admin maintenance over one subaccount. It first runs the same mask pass as `POST /bank-accounts/link-enrolled-cards`, then each action the request asks for. The actions create cards on the cards platform or rewrite stored rows, so this route needs `banking:admin`, while the mask pass alone stays on `link-enrolled-cards` at `banking:write`. The caller's account comes from its token: it can run maintenance on any subaccount of its own account, and a subaccount of another account simply matches nothing (an empty result, not a `403`).

Three optional actions, each off by default:

- `mint: true` runs the completion-time mint pass over the subaccount's credit bank accounts that a completed link left without a card (the same-last-4 American Express case), so each gains a bank-feed card. Idempotent: an account that already holds a minted card is skipped.
- `backfillJunctionLast4: true` fills, for the subaccount's card links, the last 4 each link answers to where it is still unknown, from the cards directory. Idempotent.
- `createCardholderCards: true` runs, now and for this subaccount only, what a scheduled job does every 30 minutes: it gives each cardholder behind a pooled American Express billing account (a supplementary card that is not its own Plaid account) a bank-feed card of their own, with the cardholder's name, so their transactions can be emitted on that card. It does nothing unless Astrada has switched the feature on for the subaccount; the switches are set by Astrada only, from inside the platform, and no request can set them. Idempotent: a cardholder who already has a card is never given another.

The actions run in the order above, after the mask pass. If the cards directory cannot be read, the mask pass links nothing and still returns `201`; each action then reads the directory again on its own and says so in its result (`directoryUnavailable`), or, for `mint` with accounts to screen, fails rather than mint unscreened. Any step that fails returns `400` and runs nothing after it (steps before it have done their work, and every step is idempotent, so the request can simply be repeated). Emits no webhook from banking; a card created here produces the cards platform's usual card-subscription events.

201.description: Maintenance executed. Maps each bank account that gained links to the card ids linked in this run (empty object when nothing matched). The other fields appear only for the actions the request asked for.

Returns a list of bank subscriptions (active connections to financial institutions) under the account.

post.summary: Simulate an American Express bulk file (sandbox only)
post.description:
Works in the sandbox only (`https://api.sandbox.astrada.co`). Production
has no such call.

Creates a simulated American Express bulk-enrollment file, plus a
companion settlement file when `transactionsPerCard` is above `0`, and
processes it as if American Express had delivered it. The call returns
`202 Accepted` at once; enrolled cards appear as card subscriptions when
processing finishes, and their settlements follow shortly after.

A bulk feed must already exist for the `networkReference`, created with
`POST /network-bulk-feeds`.

`cardCount` replays the fixed head of the sandbox account pool (encrypted
feeds; for tokenized feeds see below): the same accounts every call, so once
enrolled in a subaccount they deduplicate (no new
`cardsubscription.created`), exactly like a file that is delivered twice.
`newCardCount` draws accounts the subaccount has never seen from a
reserved pool, so every call enrolls that many new cards. All included
cards get `transactionsPerCard` transactions with fresh ids and recent
dates, so repeat calls always produce `transaction.*` webhooks.

For a feed registered `tokenized` (see `panFormat` on
`POST /network-bulk-feeds`), `cardCount` draws American Express network
tokens instead of raw card numbers, and `newCardCount` is not supported
(there is no tokenized new-card pool).

202.description:
Accepted. The simulated file was created and is processed
asynchronously. The response has no body.

post.summary: Simulate a pulled Visa bulk feed delivery (sandbox only)
post.description:
Works in the sandbox only (`https://api.sandbox.astrada.co`). Production
has no such call.

Simulates one delivery on a Visa bulk feed of `type: VBDS`, the kind
Astrada pulls from Visa instead of receiving a file. The delivery enrolls
cards and, when `transactionsPerCard` is above `0`, adds settlements for
them. The call returns `202 Accepted` at once; enrolled cards appear as
card subscriptions when processing finishes.

A bulk feed must already exist for the `networkReference`, created with
`POST /network-bulk-feeds`; otherwise the call returns `400`.

`cardCount` replays the fixed head of the sandbox card pool: the same
cards every call, so once enrolled in a subaccount they deduplicate (no
new `cardsubscription.created`), exactly like a delivery that arrives
twice. `newCardCount` draws cards the subaccount has never seen from a
reserved pool, so every call enrolls that many new cards. All included
cards get `transactionsPerCard` transactions with fresh ids and recent
dates, so repeat calls always produce `transaction.*` webhooks.

asynchronously. The response has no body.

`POST /network-bulk-feeds`.

cards every call, so once enrolled in a subaccount they deduplicate (no new
`cardsubscription.created`), exactly like a file that is delivered twice.

`transactionsPerCard` transactions with fresh references and recent dates,
so repeat calls always produce `transaction.*` webhooks.

asynchronously. The response has no body.

Works in the sandbox only (`https://api.sandbox.astrada.co`). Production

Runs a predefined transaction scenario, such as a purchase followed by a
refund, on an enrolled card. The call publishes every transaction message
of the scenario as if a card network had sent them and returns `202
Accepted` with their ids. The transactions arrive asynchronously through
the `transaction.created` and `transaction.updated` webhooks.

The call does not look the card up first: well-formed ids return `202`
even when they do not name an enrolled card of your account. If no

transaction message, an authorization or a settlement, as if a card
network had sent it. Follow it with
`POST /simulate/transactions/{transactionId}` to add further messages to
the transaction.

expand-card-subscription.name: expand
expand-card-subscription.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to embed on each card subscription under `_embedded`, so one call returns
the subscription together with its card and cardholder instead of a `GET /cards/{cardId}` and a
`GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` per item.

- `card` embeds the card exactly as `GET /cards/{cardId}` serves it and requires the `cards:read` scope.
- `cardholder` embeds the cardholder exactly as `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` serves it and requires the
  `cardholder:read` scope.

A request naming a resource its credentials cannot read is refused with `403`. When a related resource does not
exist (for example a card without cardholder data), its key is absent from `_embedded`; `_links` are unchanged.

Send one comma-separated value (`expand=card,cardholder`). A repeated `expand` key, an empty value or an unknown
value is refused with `400`.

Embed the card's related `cardholder` resource under `_embedded` so one call returns the card
together with its cardholder instead of a follow-up `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder`.

- `cardholder` embeds the cardholder exactly as `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` serves it and

A request asking to expand a resource its credentials cannot read is refused with `403`
(`Missing scope 'cardholder:read'`). When the card has no cardholder, the `cardholder` key is absent
from `_embedded`; `_links` are unchanged.

Send `expand=cardholder`. A repeated `expand` key, an empty value or an unknown value is refused
with `400`.

Exact, case-sensitive match. Requires the `cardholder:read` scope.

transaction-legal-entity-id.name: legalEntityId
transaction-legal-entity-id.description: Only transactions whose card's cardholder belonged to this legal entity (`corporate.legalEntity.id`) on the transaction date (the value `expand=cardholder` returns on that transaction; the `expand` parameter defines the date), not the legal entity it belongs to now. Exact, case-sensitive match. URL-encode the value: a space is `%20` (or `+`), for example `legalEntityName=Astrada%20Life`. A literal `+` is read as a space, so send a `+` in the name as `%2B`. Requires the `cardholder:read` scope.

expand-transaction.name: expand
expand-transaction.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to embed on the transaction under `_embedded`, so one call
returns the transaction together with its card subscription, card and cardholder instead of follow-up
calls to `GET /card-subscriptions?cardId=`, `GET /cards/{cardId}` and `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder`.

- `cardSubscription` embeds the card subscription exactly as `GET /card-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`
  serves it (without its own `_embedded`) and requires the `card-subscriptions:read` scope.
- `card` embeds the transaction's card exactly as `GET /cards/{cardId}` serves it (without its own
  `_embedded`) and requires the `cards:read` scope.
- `cardholder` embeds the card's cardholder as `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` serves it, with one
  difference: `corporate` is the cardholder's corporate as of the transaction (see below). Requires the
  `cardholder:read` scope.

Each value is checked separately: a request asking to expand a resource its credentials cannot read is
refused with `403`.

The embedded subscription is the card's subscription in the transaction's sub-account: the one from
the transaction's network bulk feed when the transaction has a `networkBulkFeedId`, otherwise the
card's current subscription, otherwise its most recent one.

`cardSubscription` and `card` show their **current** values, not the values they had when the transaction
happened. So does the cardholder, except for `cardholder.corporate`: its `id`, `employeeId`,
`alternativeEmployeeId` and `legalEntity` are the values in effect on the transaction's
`transactionOccurrenceDate` (through the end of that UTC day), or at the transaction's `createdAt` when
`transactionOccurrenceDate` is null. A card that moved to another company or legal entity after the
transaction therefore still shows the one it belonged to at the time. `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`,
`postalCode`, `corporate.networkToken`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are the cardholder's current values. Changes
are dated by when Astrada received them from the card network or through the API. For a transaction
dated before Astrada started recording the card's corporate history, the earliest recorded values are
returned instead. Either way, a value that was not set in the values returned is null, or for
`legalEntity` absent.

A key is present only when it was requested and the related resource exists, and it is never null.
A transaction with no card (`cardId` is null, for example a bank-sourced transaction with no linked
card) has no `cardSubscription`, `card` or `cardholder`. A card without cardholder data has no
`cardholder`. A card that `GET /cards/{cardId}` no longer returns (it responds `404`, for example
because all of its card subscriptions were deleted) is not embedded: both `card` and `cardholder` are
absent. `_links` are unchanged. Without `expand`, `_embedded` is absent. Whether `cardholder` is embedded
is decided on the card and cardholder as they are now, not as of the transaction's date.

Send one comma-separated value (`expand=cardSubscription,card,cardholder`). A repeated `expand` key,
an empty value or an unknown value is refused with `400`.

bank-link-id.name: bankLinkId
bank-link-id.description: The client-provided identifier of the bank link.

bin-required.name: bin
bin-required.description:
The first 6 to 11 digits of the card number. Send digits only, and never the full card
number. Input that is shorter than 6 digits, longer than 11 digits, or contains anything
other than digits is rejected with `400`; longer input is not truncated.

For a Mastercard card, send more digits (up to 11) for a more precise issuer country. 11
digits gives the most precise answer.

verifications.description: The link to this card's 3-D Secure verifications (`/card-verifications/3ds?cardId=`). Useful when a subscription is stuck at `reqSCA` to inspect why verification failed.
