bankAccount.description: The link to the bank account this subscription's card was materialized from (`/bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}`). Present only when the `enrollmentType` is `bank-feed`; the bank-connected analog of `networkBulkFeed`. Not present for `cardholder-single` or `network-bulk` subscriptions.

cardholder-corporate-legalEntity.description: The legal entity the card belongs to in the card network's company hierarchy. Visa VCF: the hierarchy node directly under the root. Mastercard SmartData: the corporation the card is filed under. American Express: the legal company the card is issued under (the Basic Control Account is a division within a company, not a legal entity, and is not used here). Present only when the card network supplies one; absent otherwise, never null. `id` and `name` are each present only when the network supplies them, and at least one of them is always present. Once set it is kept until the network sends a new one. The same entity sent again with a field left out keeps that field: entities match on `id` when both have one, otherwise on `name`; a different entity replaces the stored one entirely. When the cardholder is embedded on a transaction, this is the value as of the transaction's date (see `corporate`).

id.description: The network's identifier for the legal entity, an opaque string. Present only when the network supplies one (Visa VCF currently always does; Mastercard SmartData files usually carry none and American Express files never do); absent otherwise, never null. Filter by `legalEntityName` when it is absent.

name.description: The legal entity's name as provided by the card network. Present only when the network supplies a name (Visa VCF and Mastercard SmartData currently always do; American Express sends the legal company name; when the file leaves it blank, `legalEntity` is omitted entirely); absent otherwise, never null. Filter by `legalEntityId` when it is absent.

cardholder-corporate.description:
The company the cardholder belongs to, as the bank or card network supplies it in a network bulk feed, unless it was set with `PATCH /cards/{cardId}/cardholder`. See the [Glossary](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/glossary) for the terms used here.

On `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` this is the current value. When the cardholder is embedded on a transaction (`expand=cardholder`, or the transaction webhooks), `corporate` is the value in effect on the transaction's `transactionOccurrenceDate` (through the end of that UTC day), or at the transaction's `createdAt` when that is null; the other cardholder fields stay current. The one exception inside `corporate` is `networkToken`, which is always the card's current value.

alternativeEmployeeId.description: An alternative employee identifier, typically configured for specific enterprise integrations.

employeeId.description: The unique identifier of the employee

id.description:
The **company ID**: the identifier the bank or card network gives the cardholder's company in the network bulk feed. Every card from the same company carries the same value, so it is the field to group cards by company.

- **Visa (VCF and VBDS)**: the company ID, the `C` in the feed's RPIC network reference (`RegionId_ProcessorId_IssuerId_CompanyId`), always its last segment. For the feed `1_123_45_6789` (or the VCF PIC form `123_45_6789`), `corporate.id` is `6789`.
- **Mastercard (SmartData)**: the company ID from the file, which Mastercard calls the corporation number.
- **American Express**: the company ID, the 6-digit corporate ID (CID), such as `014640`. For a feed whose network reference is the CID, `corporate.id` is that same value.

`null` when the feed does not supply one. The legal entity within the company is in `legalEntity`.

networkToken.description: The network token the card network issued for the card, for a tokenized American Express card. It is the same token the network sends you in its own files, so it is a stable identifier for matching the cardholder to your records. On these cards the card's `first6digits` and `last4digits` are the token's digits, not the physical card's. Present only for tokenized American Express cards; absent otherwise, never null. Always the card's current value, also when the cardholder is embedded on a transaction.

cardholder.description:
The person a card belongs to: their name, email address and postal code, and their company details in
`corporate`. A card has at most one cardholder, and not every card has one. Which fields are filled depends
on how the card was enrolled:

- **Card entered by number** (the card form, or `POST /card-subscriptions`): since 10 November 2026,
  created with the card subscription, before the bank's check, from the `cardholderName` sent. When created it
  holds only `firstName` and `lastName`; `email`, `postalCode` and the ids in `corporate` (`id`,
  `employeeId`, `alternativeEmployeeId`) are `null`. A blank `cardholderName` gives no cardholder, and a
  card entered by number before 10 November 2026 got none when it was entered.
- **Network bulk feed**: created from the network's file when it carries cardholder data, with the fields
  that file carries. Which fields those are differs by network.
- **Bank sign-in**: the cardholders a bank sign-in creates are on some American Express cards only, and
  hold no company details when created. See
  [American Express cards](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/bank-linking#which-kind-of-account-is-it).

Read it with `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` (scope `cardholder:read`), or inline with `expand=cardholder`
on a card, a card subscription or a transaction. A card that has a cardholder carries a `cardholder` link
in its `_links`. For a card without one, `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` answers `404`, and `expand` on the
card or its card subscription leaves the `cardholder` key out; for a transaction, see `expand` on
`GET /transactions/{transactionId}`. In the sandbox, once a card's card subscriptions are deleted, the
cardholder answers `404` too. [Cards](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/cards#cardholder) lists the fields and
what each way of enrolling fills.

firstName.description: The first name of the cardholder. When created for a card entered by number, every word of the `cardholderName` sent but the last; `null` when that name is one word.

lastName.description: The last name of the cardholder. When created for a card entered by number, the last word of the `cardholderName` sent.

postalCode.description: Cardholder postal code as provided by the card network. Format varies by country; no validation or normalization is applied.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

card-embedded.description:
Related resources inlined on request with the `expand` query parameter (`?expand=cardholder`).
The `cardholder` key is present only when it was requested and the cardholder exists; its body
is identical to the one served by `GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder`. Absent entirely when
`expand` is not sent.

id.description: The unique identifier of this card entity.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

expiryMonth.description: The month that the card will expire in MM format.

expiryYear.description: The year that the card will expire in YYYY format.

first6digits.description:
The first 6 digits of the card number (PAN). Nullable for bank-derived cards
(created from a bank connection, where the full PAN is never seen); populated when
known (e.g. the SDK captured the BIN before pivoting to the bank flow) and attached
when the card is later PAN-enrolled (upgrade-in-place keeps the same card id).

last4digits.description: The last 4 digits of the card number (PAN).

network.description:
The card network that processes payments for this card. `amex` and `null` occur only
on bank-derived cards: Amex-institution connections mint `amex`; other institutions
cannot reveal the network from bank data, so it stays `null` until the card is
PAN-enrolled (upgrade-in-place).

country.description: The country of issuance for this card following ISO 3166 alpha-3.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

card-subscription-embedded.description:
Related resources inlined on request with the `expand` query parameter (`?expand=card,cardholder`). A key is
present only when it was requested and the related resource exists; each embedded body is identical to the one
served by the resource's own endpoint. Absent entirely when `expand` is not sent.

card-subscription-deactivation-reason.description:
Why a card subscription was deactivated, as given by the customer in the deactivation request.

- `card_lost`: the cardholder lost the card.
- `card_stolen`: the card was stolen.
- `card_replaced`: the card was reissued or replaced with a new card number.
- `card_closed`: the issuer or bank closed the card or its account.
- `cardholder_offboarded`: the cardholder no longer works for the business.
- `organization_offboarded`: the business no longer uses your platform.
- `suspected_fraud`: the card is suspected of fraudulent use.
- `duplicate_enrollment`: the card was enrolled more than once.
- `no_longer_needed`: the card no longer needs to share data.
- `other`: any other reason.

New values may be added later. Handle a value you don't recognize as `other`.

id.description: The unique identifier of this subscription entity.

accountId.description: The unique identifier of the account related to this entity.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

cardId.description: The unique identifier of the card related to this entity.

customerReferenceId.description: An optional id in UUID format passed by the customer to associate a context with the subscription.

state.description:
State of the subscription. `active` and `pending` subscriptions are both considered enrolled in Astrada's
platform. A `pending` subscription is enrolled from a network roster while the card is still inactive at the
network (e.g. Mastercard Smart Data `I` status): it is customer-visible but has not yet received a
transaction. It exits only by promotion to `active` (a later roster `active` record or the card's first
clearing transaction), explicit deactivation, or expiry. Virtual cards are excluded from `pending` enrollment.

deactivationReason.description:
The reason given when this subscription was deactivated. Only present on a deactivated subscription
that was given a reason; the field is left out otherwise. New values may be added, so treat an
unknown value as `other`.

effectiveDate.description: Date and time when this card subscription will be activated and start receiving data, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

expirationDate.description: Date and time when this card subscription will become expired and stop receiving data, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

networkBulkFeedId.description: The unique identifier of the network bulk feed associated with this card subscription. Present when the `enrollmentType` is `network-bulk`, null otherwise.

bankAccountId.description: The bank account this subscription's card was originally materialized from; present only when `enrollmentType` is `bank-feed` (the analog of `networkBulkFeedId` for bank-connected enrollments). This is provenance and does not re-point if a re-link later attaches the card to a successor account; the current link surface is the bank account's `cardIds`.

enrollmentType.description: The flow that led to the creation of the card subscription. `cardholder-single` refers to enrollments where cardholders themselves are responsible for inputting card data and where a single card is attempted at a time. `network-bulk` refers to enrollments where card data will be captured by Astrada using network data sources (eg Mastercard Smart Data) and where many cards may be attempted at once. `bank-feed` refers to cards materialized from a bank connection (e.g. American Express via the hosted bank-linking flow); the bank-side analog of `network-bulk`, with `bankAccountId` as the back-reference.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

totalItems.description: Total number of card subscriptions matching the search criteria

validation-problem.description: A `400 Bad Request` body. `errors`, when present, lists each problem found in the request.

title.description: A short summary of the status, `Bad Request` on this response.

problem.description:
An error body in the problem details format (`application/problem+json`). Every error
response without its own fields uses it.

title.description:
A short summary of the status, for example `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `Not Found` or
`Internal Server Error`. Each response's example shows its value.

deactivationReason.description:
Optional reason for the deactivation. Only accepted together with `state: deactivated`;
sending it on its own returns `400`. Returned in the `deactivationReason` field of the card subscription.

currentValue.description: Current value for the property causing the conflict

requestedValue.description: Requested value for the property causing the conflict

self.description: The link to this verification resource.

steps.description: The link to this verification's steps (`/card-verifications/3ds/{verificationId}/steps`).

currentStep.description:
The link to the step the client should execute next. Absent once the
verification reaches a terminal `state` (`completed` or `failed`).

failure-reason-acsReferences.description: 3DS ACS reference identifiers, when returned by the issuer; useful when escalating to the issuer.

failure-reason.description:
Normalized, customer-facing reason a card verification failed. Present only when the
verification `state` is `failed`. `category`, `description` and `retryable` are always
present; `issuerMessage` and `acsReferences` appear only when the issuer returned them
(typically on a frictionless decline; when the issuer renders its own challenge UI no
per-attempt message is available).

category.description:
Stable, provider-agnostic failure category an integrator can branch on without
enumerating raw issuer codes.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the failure, safe to relay to the cardholder.

retryable.description: Whether the cardholder can retry now and plausibly succeed.

issuerMessage.description: The issuer's own cardholder-facing message, when provided (frictionless declines only).

code.description:
Raw provider reason code (e.g. a 3DS `transStatusReason` or a Stripe `decline_code`),
surfaced for support escalation.

providerMessage.description:
The payment provider's cardholder-safe message for the specific failure code (e.g.
"Your card does not support this type of purchase."). Finer-grained than the
category-level `description`; absent when the provider supplied none.

adviceCode.description:
The issuer's advice code on authorization declines, verbatim from the payment
provider. Documented values: `try_again_later`, `do_not_try_again`,
`confirm_card_data`; values the provider introduces later pass through unchanged.
Absent when the issuer gave no advice (e.g. 3-D Secure authentication failures).

id.description: The unique identifier of the Verification entity.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

cardId.description: The unique identifier of the card related to this entity.

currentStepId.description:
The identifier of the next step the client should execute. `null` when
the verification has no follow-up step; typically because the issuer
supports frictionless authentication, or because the card did not
require interactive 3DS. When `null`, `state` will be `completed` on the
creation response and clients should not call any `/steps/...` endpoint.

On retrieved/listed verifications, `currentStepId` is also `null` with
`state: failed` when the card was declined synchronously at creation
(the creation call returned `400`, and the attempt is persisted as a
failed verification with its `failureReason`).

For the HIGHEST tier, a frictionless 3DS outcome does NOT complete the
verification: it returns `stripe-holds-pending` (the cardholder must
initiate two small verification holds via `/steps/place-holds`), which
then advances to `stripe-amount-confirm` (the cardholder reads the two
amounts back via `/steps/amount-confirm`).

clientSecret.description: Stripe SetupIntent or PaymentIntent client secret, used by the client to run `stripe.handleNextAction`. Returned whenever the verification is on the Stripe 3DS step; on the creation response (`POST /card-verifications/3ds`) and on the retrieve response (`GET /card-verifications/3ds/{verificationId}`) while `currentStepId` is `stripe-3ds`.

stripePublishableKey.description: Stripe publishable key to initialize Stripe.js on the client. Returned alongside `clientSecret` (creation response and retrieve response while `currentStepId` is `stripe-3ds`).

authenticationFlow.description:
The 3DS authentication flow attested by the issuer, surfaced at the terminal state.
`challenge` = the cardholder actively authenticated; `frictionless` = the issuer approved
without interaction; `null` = 3DS was not engaged (e.g. a low-risk automatic skip).

failureReason.description:
Normalized, customer-facing reason the verification failed. Present only when
`state` is `failed`; read it to triage the failure (category, retryability,
and the issuer's message). See the `FailureReason` schema.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

cardId.description: Identifier of the card whose attempt lockout to clear.

cleared.description:
Whether an active lock actually existed and was cleared. `false`
when the card had no active lock (the idempotent no-op case).

totalItems.description: Total number of cards matching the search criteria

cardholder-update-params-corporate.description: The corporate entity that this cardholder is associated with. `legalEntity` is set by the card network and cannot be changed here: it is ignored if sent, and the stored value is kept.

id.description: The company ID to store on the cardholder, the same value a network bulk feed supplies. See `cardholder.corporate.id`.

employeeId.description: The unique identifier of the employee

alternativeEmployeeId.description: An alternative employee identifier, typically configured for specific enterprise integrations.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to the card

firstName.description: The first name of the cardholder

lastName.description: The last name of the cardholder

postalCode.description: Cardholder postal code. Format varies by country; no validation or normalization is applied.

bin.description: The card's Bank Identification Number (BIN), consisting of the first 6 to 11 digits of the card number. Providing more digits yields more precise results: for example, two cards that share the same 6-digit BIN may support different enrollment methods. Send as many digits as you have, up to 11. For Mastercard, 8 digits or fewer can match several card ranges; when those ranges disagree, `bulkLikelihood` is capped at `medium` (a `proven` BIN keeps `proven`), and at `medium` a Mastercard card is not offered `network-bulk`.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount the card would enroll under. With it, the response adds `singleDecision` when the subaccount's controls can be run. It must be one of your account's subaccounts, otherwise the request gets `400`. With an enrollment link session's token it must be the session's own subaccount, otherwise the request gets `403`.

enrollment-methods-result-singleDecision.description: Whether the subaccount named in `subaccountId` can enroll this card one at a time. Present only when the request names a `subaccountId` and that subaccount's controls could be run for these digits. When they could not (for example, the subaccount could not be read, or, in sandbox, the digits match test cards of more than one card type), `singleDecision` is omitted and the rest of the response is the one given without `subaccountId`.

allowed.description: `true` when every single-enrollment control passes for the subaccount and the card's own `singleEligible`, as answered without `subaccountId`, is `true`.

reason.description: Why single enrollment is refused. Present only when `allowed` is `false`. A control's refusal is named before `coverage`. Each control's reason stands for the refusal that control gives on `POST /card-subscriptions`, shown in parentheses. `bank-enrollment-required`: the subaccount's `enrollmentPolicy.bankEnrollment` is `amex-visa` and this Visa card is not classified as business (`card_subscription.subaccount_blocking_card_type` with `reasonCode` `card_subscription.bank_enrollment_required`). `card-type`: the subaccount's single-enrollment `blockedCardTypes` holds the card's type (`card_subscription.subaccount_blocking_card_type`). `funding-type`: its `blockedFundingCardTypes` holds the card's funding type (`card_subscription.subaccount_blocking_card_funding_type`). `issuer-country`: `enforceIssuerCountry` is on and the card's issuing country is unknown or not one of the subaccount's single-enrollment countries (`card_subscription.subaccount_blocking_card_country`). `network-rule`: a rule in the subaccount's `networkBlockedCards` matches the card (`card_subscription.network_blocking_card`). `coverage`: every control passes, but the card's own `singleEligible` is `false`, for example for any American Express card.

enrollment-methods-result-binInfo.description: Best-effort card metadata for the looked-up BIN, resolved server-side. Present only when the issuer name is known and omitted otherwise; the other fields are best-effort and may each be omitted even when `binInfo` is present. Lets integrators read this data without the `cards:read` scope that `GET /bin-lookup` requires (it rides on this endpoint's `enrollment-methods:write` scope); the SDK surfaces it on the bulk-enrollment success payload.

issuerName.description: The issuing bank's name for this BIN.

issuerCountry.description: The country of the issuing bank following ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, for example `USA`. Omitted when the reference data does not record it.

type.description: The card type (e.g., COMMERCIAL, CORPORATE, CONSUMER, SMALL_BUSINESS). Omitted when the reference data does not classify the BIN.

fundingType.description: The card funding type (e.g., prepaid, debit, credit). Omitted when the reference data does not classify the BIN.

cardCategory.description: The card's classification, with the values of `cardCategory` on `GET /bin-lookup`. More specific than `type`, and set for many BINs where `type` is omitted. `UNKNOWN` means the card data does not classify the BIN. Omitted when there is no value. For Mastercard it is present only when the response falls back to stored card data.

availableEnrollmentMethods.description: The enrollment methods this card can use: `network-bulk` when `bulkLikelihood` is present and not `none` (for Visa and Mastercard cards, only `high` or `proven`), and `cardholder-single` when `singleEligible` is `true`. Empty when neither applies, for example for a card from a country Astrada doesn't cover for its network.

bulkLikelihood.description: Graded likelihood that network-bulk enrollment will succeed for this BIN. A country-coverage veto forces `none`. Omitted when it could not be determined for this request; `unavailable` then lists it. `none` is only returned when it was established, never because the data was unavailable. Whether `network-bulk` is offered is in `availableEnrollmentMethods`: for Visa and Mastercard cards it needs `high` or `proven`.

singleEligible.description: Whether cardholder-single enrollment is supported for this BIN. When the response has `singleDecision`, it equals `singleDecision.allowed`.

unavailable.description: Response fields whose value could not be determined for this request, for example when live card data was temporarily unavailable and the stored card data doesn't decide the grade. Today it can only contain `bulkLikelihood`; more values may be added, so ignore any you don't recognize. Omitted when every field was determined.

via.description:
- `api`: `POST /enrollment-links` with `subaccounts:write`.
- `staff`: `POST /enrollment-links` with Astrada's `accounts:write`.
- `sdk`: `POST /subaccounts/{subaccountId}/team-link`, the route for the SDK's
  "Invite your team" ending.

clientId.description: The client ID of the credential that created the link, when known.

enrollment-link.description:
An enrollment link to the Astrada-hosted page where people enroll their own cards into
one subaccount. The link's `url` is returned only by the request that creates it.

id.description: The link's identifier.

kind.description:
- `cardholder`: a personal link for one employee. It allows up to 5 session starts and
  is used up by the first session that completes something.
- `team`: a link to share with a team. Every session start counts as a use, up to
  `maxUses`.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount that cards enrolled through the link join.

startingPoint.description: Where the hosted page starts. Only `card` is available now; links made before the field existed read as `card`.

state.description:
- `active`: sessions can start.
- `used`: a personal link whose session completed something.
- `revoked`: revoked with `POST /enrollment-links/{linkId}/revoke` or by deleting its
  subaccount. Team links revoked by the former five-active-link limit on
  `POST /subaccounts/{subaccountId}/team-link` stay revoked.
- `expired`: an active link past `expiresAt`.

expiresAt.description: After this time no session starts from the link.

maxUses.description: 1 on a personal link. On a team link, the session starts it allows.

uses.description: On a team link, the sessions started so far. On a personal link, 1 once it is used, otherwise 0.

starts.description: The sessions started from the link so far.

customerReferenceId.description: The reference given when the link was created. Absent when none was given.

platformName.description:
The platform name given when the link was created. Absent when none was given. The
hosted page ignores it once the account has a brand profile.

organizationName.description: The organization name given when the link was created. Absent when none was given.

usedAt.description: When a personal link was used up.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount that cards enrolled through the link join. It must be one of your subaccounts.

kind.description: `cardholder` for a personal link, `team` for a team link.

customerReferenceId.description:
Your reference for the link, such as the employee a personal link is for. It
must be a UUID, as `customerReferenceId` on `POST /card-subscriptions` is;
any other value answers `400`. A session from the link can create card
subscriptions only with this reference.

platformName.description:
The platform's name, shown on the hosted page. Letters, digits, spaces and
`. , & ' ’ ( ) - _ + ! # @` only, with at least one letter or digit;
surrounding spaces are trimmed. Default: your account's name. A name
that is a well-known brand, such as a card network or a large bank, answers
`400` `LINK_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED`. Once Astrada has set a brand profile for your
account, the hosted pages show its name and ignore this one.

startingPoint.description:
Where the hosted page starts. Only `card` is available now; any other value
answers `400`.

expiresInHours.description:
How long the link can start sessions. Default: 168 (7 days) for a personal
link, 336 (14 days) for a team link.

maxUses.description:
Team links only: the session starts the link allows. Default: 50. On a
personal link it answers `400`.

url.description: The link to send. Its secret follows `#`.

enrollment-link-session-outcome.description:
What the hosted page reported when the session completed. A session completes something
when it reports at least one id.

The ids are as the page sent them: nothing checks them against the card or bank APIs.
The `cardsubscription` webhooks are the source of truth for what was enrolled. When the
link has a `customerReferenceId`, the card subscriptions created through it carry that
reference.

subscriptionIds.description: Card subscriptions the page reports it created.

cardIds.description: Cards the page reports it enrolled.

bankLinkIds.description: Bank links the page reports it completed.

summary.description:
Up to 10 counts the page reports. Each name is 1 to 40 letters and digits and starts
with a letter.

enrollment-link-session.description: A session started from an enrollment link, as the hosted page ran it.

id.description: The session's identifier.

state.description:
- `open`: started and not yet completed.
- `completed`: the page reported the session's outcome.
- `expired`: an open session past `expiresAt`. It can no longer complete.

sessions.description: The sessions started from the link, oldest first.

network-reference.description:
The identifier associated with the card network's bulk enrollment feed. Its format depends on the network.
For Amex, the Recipient ID in the format 'R{RecipientId}', such as 'R123456', or the 6-digit Amex corporate ID (CID), such as '014640'.
For Mastercard, the Delivery ID, such as 'G1234567'; its format is not checked.
For Visa-VBDS, the RPIC: four numeric parts joined by underscores, 'RegionId_ProcessorId_IssuerId_CompanyId', such as '1_123_45_6789'.
For Visa-VCF, the same RPIC 'RegionId_ProcessorId_IssuerId_CompanyId', such as '1_123_45_6789' (the region segment is ignored), or the 3-segment PIC form 'ProcessorId_IssuerId_CompanyId', such as '123_45_6789'.
For Visa, a part that is not all digits is refused with `400`, naming the part. Spaces around each part and leading zeros are removed before the reference is stored.
For more details on our bulk enrollment process, refer to [this guide](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/network-bulk-enrollment).

id.description: The unique identifier of this network bulk feed entity.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

network.description: The network where the feed belongs.

state.description:
The state of the network bulk feed entity.

> **Note**: The `failed` state is currently only applicable to VISA bulk feeds.

type.description:
The feed's delivery rail. Always set for `AMEX` (`GL`) and `MASTERCARD`
(`SMARTDATA`), and for a `VISA` feed created with an explicit type.

`null` while a `VISA` feed created without a type is still discovering
its rail: it stays `submitted` and becomes `VBDS` or `VCF` (and
`active`) as soon as a VBDS connection or a VCF file confirms the rail.
The `networkbulkfeed.statechanged` webhook for that transition carries
the resolved value.

panFormat.description:
The PAN format of the feed's card data: `encrypted` (raw PAN) or
`tokenized` (Amex network token / `tokenizedId`).

Outside the sandbox environment this is derived internally at feed
creation (determined by Astrada from the network/file signals, never
accepted on the create request) and defaults to `encrypted`. In the
sandbox environment it may be set explicitly on the create request for
`type: GL` (AMEX) feeds only, so the Simulate flow can register a
tokenized feed (see `panFormat` on `POST /network-bulk-feeds`). It is
always returned on the feed representation.

errorReason.description:
A human-readable reason explaining why the bulk feed failed. Present when `state` is `failed`.
For a `VISA` feed still discovering its rail (`type` is `null`, `state` is `submitted`) it may
also carry the latest error reported by one rail, prefixed with that rail (for example `VBDS: ...`);
the feed keeps waiting for the other rail and the field is cleared when the feed becomes `active`.

> **Note**: Currently only applicable to VISA bulk feeds.

expectedCardCount.description:
The expected number of cards that will be enrolled under this bulk feed, as provided at creation time.
Only present when the feed was created with this field.

transactionStartDate.description:
Transactions posted on or after this calendar date are ingested for this
feed's deliveries, replacing the default 15-day ingestion window.
Currently supported for SMARTDATA feeds only. Only present when set;
when absent, the default 15-day window applies. The comparison is
calendar-day based in UTC: the network's posting date is a date-only
field, so the cutoff is the start of the stated day with no
local-timezone adjustment.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

totalItems.description: Total number of network bulk feeds

network-bulk-feed-create-common.description:
The fields every network's bulk feed create body shares. Some apply to one network only; the
API rejects them with a 400 for any other network or feed type:

| Field | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `networkReference`, `subaccountId`, `networkBulkEnrollmentId`, `expectedCardCount` | Every network |
| `transactionStartDate` | `MASTERCARD` (type `SMARTDATA`) |
| `cardCount`, `newCards` | `VISA` with type `VBDS` or no `type`, sandbox only |
| `panFormat` | `AMEX` (type `GL`), sandbox only |

subaccountId.description: The subaccount identifier

networkBulkEnrollmentId.description:
Optional. The network bulk enrollment (`POST /network-bulk-enrollments`)
this feed fulfils. The enrollment must exist on this account, its
`subaccountId` and `network` must equal the body's, and its `state` must
be `requested` or `feed-created` (re-registering after a failed feed is
allowed). Any mismatch is rejected with a 400 whose `detail` reads
`networkBulkEnrollmentId does not match this subaccount and network`.
When the feed is created, the enrollment's `networkBulkFeedId` is set and
its state moves to `feed-created`; the link lives on the enrollment, so
the feed representation is unchanged. A duplicate feed still answers 409
and leaves the enrollment untouched.

expectedCardCount.description:
The expected number of cards that will be enrolled under this bulk feed.
Optional. When provided, the value is echoed back on the response and on the
`networkbulkfeed.statechanged` webhook payload.

transactionStartDate.description:
Optional. Transactions posted on or after this calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`,
a valid date, not in the future) are taken in for this feed's deliveries,
replacing the default window, which keeps only transactions posted on or
after the date 15 days before each file's delivery date (in UTC). On a file
that serves several subaccounts, the earliest window among them applies to
the whole file. Currently supported for `SMARTDATA` feeds only; requests
containing this field for any other feed type are rejected with a 400. When
unset, the 15-day window applies. Also
settable later via `PATCH /network-bulk-feeds/{networkBulkFeedId}`.
The comparison is calendar-day based in UTC: the network's posting date is
a date-only field, so a value of e.g. `2026-06-30` includes every
transaction whose posting date is 2026-06-30 or later, with no
local-timezone adjustment.

cardCount.description:
Sandbox only. The number of synthetic Visa cards to create when this
bulk feed is created in the sandbox environment. The cards are drawn
from the head of Astrada's published sandbox Visa test-card pool:
the same cards every feed, deduplicated once enrolled (matching the
`cardCount` field on the `SimulateBulkFeedFile*` operations). Only valid
for pulled Visa feeds: `type: VBDS`, or a `VISA` feed sent without
`type`. Requests containing this field outside the sandbox
environment, or for any other feed type, are rejected with a 400.
When omitted on such a feed in sandbox, 5 starter cards are created.

newCards.description:
Deprecated alias of `cardCount`; use `cardCount` instead. When both
fields are provided, `cardCount` takes precedence. Same constraints
and behavior.

panFormat.description:
Sandbox only. Selects how card numbers arrive for this feed:
`encrypted` (raw PAN) or `tokenized` (Amex network token /
`tokenizedId`). Only valid for `type: GL` (AMEX) feeds.
Requests containing this field outside the sandbox
environment, or for any non-GL feed type, are rejected with
a 400. When omitted, the feed defaults to `encrypted`.

network.description: The network that the feed belongs

type.description: The type of card network's bulk enrollment feed

network.description: The network that the feed belongs

type.description: The type of card network's bulk enrollment feed

network.description: The network that the feed belongs

type.description:
Optional. The Visa rail this feed is delivered on. Omit it and
Astrada discovers the rail: the feed is registered on both VBDS
and VCF, `type` is `null` while the feed is `submitted`, and it
becomes `VBDS` or `VCF` when the first delivery (a VBDS
connection or a VCF file) confirms the rail. Pass `VBDS` or `VCF`
to pin the feed to one rail instead. Without a type the
`networkReference` must be the full RPIC
(`RegionId_ProcessorId_IssuerId_CompanyId`).

network-bulk-feed-create-params.description:
The body of a new network bulk feed. `network` picks the shape: `AMEX` (type `GL`),
`MASTERCARD` (type `SMARTDATA`) or `VISA` (type `VBDS` or `VCF`, or omitted).
A few shared fields apply to one network only; see the table on the shared fields.

transactionStartDate.description:
Transactions posted on or after this calendar date
(`YYYY-MM-DD`, a valid date, not in the future) are taken in
for this feed's deliveries, replacing the default window, which
keeps only transactions posted on or after the date 15 days
before each file's delivery date (in UTC). On a file that
serves several subaccounts, the earliest window among them
applies to the whole file. Currently supported for `SMARTDATA`
feeds only. The comparison is calendar-day based in UTC: the
network's posting date is a date-only field, so a value of
e.g. `2026-06-30` includes every transaction whose posting
date is 2026-06-30 or later, with no local-timezone
adjustment.

expectedCardCount.description: The expected number of cards that will be enrolled under this bulk feed.

network-bulk-enrollment-create-params-bi.description:
Optional. The issuer details shown to the person submitting the kickoff, in
the `GET /bin-lookup` vocabulary. Stored as a display snapshot only; every
field is optional.

issuerName.description: The name of the issuing bank.

issuerCountry.description: The country of the issuing bank, ISO 3166 alpha-3. Stored as sent; its format is not checked. `GET /bin-lookup` gives it as ISO 3166 alpha-3.

fundingType.description: The card funding type, for example `CREDIT`.

legalName.description: The company's legal name, exactly as it reads on the card agreement.

network-bulk-enrollment-create-params-ca.description: The card program administrator. Astrada keeps this person engaged throughout onboarding.

network-bulk-bank-contact-params.description: Optional. The company's relationship contact at the issuing bank.

network-bulk-enrollment-create-params-co.description: The card admin's approval for the company and Astrada to start bulk enrollment with the bank, including contacting the bank on the company's behalf.

accepted.description: Must be `true`. The request is rejected with a 400 otherwise.

version.description: Your own id for the consent wording that was accepted, for example `kickoff-consent-v2`. Stored as an opaque string.

requestId.description:
Optional. Your idempotency key for this enrollment, unique per account. Repeating the
request with a `requestId` that was already used returns the stored enrollment, whole
and unchanged, with `200` instead of creating a second one with `201`. A request
without a `requestId` is never a replay: it creates a new enrollment unless its
program already has an open kickoff, which answers `200` with that kickoff's summary.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount the card program enrolls into. Must belong to the calling account.

network.description: The network of the card program.

bin.description: The leading 6 to 11 digits of the card that opened the kickoff.

cardCountBand.description: Optional. The estimated number of cards in the program, as a band. An estimate helps the bank size the file.

cardCount.description: Optional. The estimated number of cards in the program. When sent, it decides the stored `cardCountBand`, even if `cardCountBand` is also sent.

outreach.description:
Who contacts the bank. `astrada`: Astrada reaches out to the bank, copying the
company and the card admin. `self`: the company emails the bank itself and
copies onboarding@astrada.co so Astrada can guide the setup.

customerReferenceId.description: Optional. Your own id for this enrollment, echoed back on the resource.

networkBulkFeed.description:
The network bulk feed registered against this enrollment
(`/network-bulk-feeds/{networkBulkFeedId}`). Present once `state` is
`feed-created`, absent before that.

network-bulk-enrollment-binInfo.description:
A snapshot of the issuer details shown to the person who submitted the kickoff,
kept for display only. `null` when the request carried none. The fields use the
`GET /bin-lookup` vocabulary.

issuerName.description: The name of the issuing bank.

issuerCountry.description: The country of the issuing bank, ISO 3166 alpha-3.

fundingType.description: The card funding type, for example `CREDIT`.

legalName.description: The legal name of the company whose card program is being enrolled.

network-bulk-enrollment-cardAdmin.description: The card program administrator. Astrada keeps this person engaged throughout onboarding.

network-bulk-bank-contact.description: The company's relationship contact at the issuing bank. `null` when not provided.

acceptedAt.description: When the consent was recorded, which is the server time of the create request, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

version.description: The version of the consent wording that was accepted, as sent by the client (for example `kickoff-consent-v1`).

id.description: The unique identifier of this network bulk enrollment.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount the card program enrolls into.

network.description: The network of the card program.

bin.description: The leading 6 to 11 digits of the card that opened the kickoff, exactly as submitted.

cardCountBand.description: The estimated number of cards in the program, as a band. `null` when not provided.

outreach.description:
Who contacts the bank. `astrada`: Astrada reaches out to the bank, copying the
company and the card admin. `self`: the company emails the bank itself and copies
onboarding@astrada.co so Astrada can guide the setup.

state.description:
`requested` until a network bulk feed is registered with this enrollment's id,
then `feed-created`. Astrada does not set `cancelled` today. A kickoff that is never
followed by a feed keeps `requested`, also after its 90 days (see
`POST /network-bulk-enrollments`).

networkBulkFeedId.description: The network bulk feed registered with this enrollment's id on `POST /network-bulk-feeds`. `null` until then.

customerReferenceId.description: An optional id passed by the customer to associate a context with the enrollment. `null` when not provided.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

self.description:
The open kickoff (`/network-bulk-enrollments/{id}`). A token with
`network-bulk-enrollments:read` or `network-bulk-feeds:read` can follow it to the
full enrollment; any other token gets `403`.

network-bulk-enrollment-summary.description:
The `200` body of `POST /network-bulk-enrollments` when the request's program already has
an open kickoff that another request wrote. A program is the calling account, the
`subaccountId`, the `network` and the first 8 digits of the `bin`. The summary names the
open kickoff and leaves out its contact details: no names, emails, bank contact, `binInfo`,
consent or outreach. `alreadyOpen` is always `true` here, and the full enrollment never
carries it, a replay of your own `requestId` included.

alreadyOpen.description: Always `true`. Tells this summary apart from the full enrollment.

id.description: The unique identifier of the open kickoff.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount of the open kickoff, the same as the request's.

network.description: The network of the open kickoff, the same as the request's.

state.description:
The open kickoff's state. `requested`: it was created less than 90 days ago and no
feed has been registered against it yet. `feed-created`: a feed was registered against
it and that feed is live.

networkBulkFeedId.description: The live feed registered against the open kickoff. `null` while the kickoff is `requested`.

requestId.description:
The `requestId` this request sent, or `null` when it sent none. It is never the
`requestId` the open kickoff was stored under.

createdAt.description: When the open kickoff was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format. Its 90-day window counts from this time.

network-bulk-enrollment-open.description:
Whether the card program has an open kickoff, the answer of
`GET /network-bulk-enrollments/open`. When it has none, the body is `{ "open": false }`
and nothing else. When it has one, the body carries only that kickoff's `enrollmentId`,
`state` and `requestedAt`: no names, emails, bank contact, `binInfo`, consent or outreach,
as the kickoff may have been sent by someone else.

open.description: Whether the program has an open kickoff, by the same rule `POST /network-bulk-enrollments` uses.

enrollmentId.description:
The open kickoff's identifier, the `id` that `POST /network-bulk-enrollments` answers
with when it finds the same kickoff. Present only when `open` is `true`.

state.description:
The open kickoff's state. `requested`: it was created less than 90 days ago and no feed
is registered yet. `feed-created`: its feed is registered and live. Present only when
`open` is `true`.

requestedAt.description:
When the open kickoff was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format. Present only when
`open` is `true`.

network-bulk-confirmation-create-params-.description:
Optional. The issuer details shown to the person who asked for the confirmation,
in the `GET /bin-lookup` vocabulary. Stored as a display snapshot only; every
field is optional.

issuerName.description: The name of the issuing bank.

plain JSON with no `_links`, as a confirmation has no GET. `alreadyOpen` is always `true`
here, and the full confirmation never carries it, a replay of your own `requestId` included.

alreadyOpen.description: Always `true`. Tells this summary apart from the full confirmation.

verification-policy.description:
Admin-managed overrides controlling how card verification is performed for an account or subaccount.
Fields are optional and nullable; absent fields leave the current value unchanged, explicit `null` clears an override.

stripeValidationLevel.description:
Routes card verifications through Stripe at the specified risk tier when set.
`null` (or absent) routes through Astrada's default card check for the network.

Tiers (increasing strictness):
  * `LOW`: internal-only; 3DS engaged only when risk/regulation requires it; issuer-unsupported
    soft declines are tolerated. Cannot be self-assigned via this endpoint.
  * `MEDIUM`: 3DS when the card provider's checks or regulation call for it; the standard tier
    to opt into.
  * `HIGH`: 3DS plus a transient authorization hold (no settled charge) and added fraud signals.
  * `HIGHEST`: 3DS challenge; if the issuer approves frictionlessly, a two-hold confirmation
    becomes a mandatory second factor. See the "HIGHEST Verification" guide.

Network note: Visa uses Stripe at every set tier; Mastercard uses its network 3DS at all tiers and
engages Stripe only at `HIGHEST` (for the two-hold second factor).

Resolution: the subaccount value is operative at request time; the account-level value is the
inheritance source applied when a subaccount is created, not a live fallback.

sandbox.description:
Test flag, settable by the customer via `PATCH /subaccounts` (and internally via the
verification-policy endpoints). When `true`, card verifications on this subaccount route KNOWN
test PANs through the card providers' test modes (real cards still go live), and new bank links
are created against Plaid Sandbox (Plaid test fixtures only; real bank credentials require the
flag off), so an integrator can deterministically test against a provisioned subaccount.
On the production API, absent / `null` / `false` → live processing only.

failedAttemptLockout.description:
When `true`, ENFORCE the cross-network attempt lockout for this tenant: a card with too many recent
hard verification failures is refused at create (`400` `verification.attempts_locked`) before any
provider is called. Account-level fallback (set once for all partner subaccounts), overridable per
subaccount. A new subaccount starts with a copy of the account's value; send `null` on the
subaccount to make it follow the account again. When the value that applies is absent, `null` or
`false`, the lockout is not enforced (failures are still recorded; only enforcement is gated).

network-blocked-card-rule.description: A platform rule that blocks enrollment of matching cards on one network.

fundingTypes.description: The BIN `fundingType` values this rule blocks. Omitted or empty means every funding type.

single-enrollment.description: Rules applied to single (SDK or API) enrollment on this network.

bulk-enrollment.description: Rules applied to bulk enrollment on this network.

subaccount-amexProduct.description: The American Express data Astrada has turned on for your account, the same on every subaccount. Only Astrada sets it; `null` means neither is on. `clearing` is transactions from American Express's card file; `realTimeAuth` is American Express authorizations as they happen (US only, by approval).

enrollment-policy.description:
Enrollment policy for an account or subaccount. Two groups of fields:

**Unified-SDK rails** (`cardEnrollment`, `bankEnrollment`, `bulkEnrollment`): which
enrollment options the unified SDK renders. Customer-writable per subaccount via
`PATCH /subaccounts/{subaccountId}`; account-level defaults are admin-managed. Rails
resolve live per field (subaccount value if set, else account) and reads are SPARSE:
only explicitly-configured rail fields are returned: an absent field means "not
configured here" and the SDK falls back to the host page's client configuration, then
its card-only default.

**Admin fields** (`linkAnotherCard`, `bankEnrollmentLocked`): `linkAnotherCard` sets whether
the success screen offers the "Link another card" CTA (shown as "Connect another company
card"), and `bankEnrollmentLocked` is the lock on `bankEnrollment`. Managed only on the
internal enrollment-policy endpoints.

Fields are optional and nullable; absent fields leave the current value unchanged, explicit
`null` clears a field.

linkAnotherCard.description:
Whether the unified SDK's success screen offers the "Link another card" secondary CTA.
Absent / `null` = not configured: enabled by default (the SDK falls back to the host
page's `open()` configuration, then its built-in default: shown).

Resolution (fail-open): subaccount GETs return the **effective**
value: `false` when either the account or the subaccount stores an explicit `false`,
`true` when either side stores `true` and neither stores `false`, omitted when neither
level sets it. Resolves live on every read (no create-time snapshot), so an account-level
`false` immediately hides the CTA for every subaccount and clearing it restores stored
subaccount values. No account gate on writes: any value is accepted on the subaccount
regardless of the account's value.

bulkEnrollmentEnabled.description:
**Deprecated:** superseded by the `bulkEnrollment` tri-state rail (the SDK maps
`true` to `suggested`, `false` to `off`, and prefers the tri-state when present).

Whether the unified enrollment SDK offers bulk-enrollment steering (BIN eligibility
check + bulk feed wizard) for this account/subaccount. `false` = the SDK skips the
eligibility check entirely and opens the card form directly (American Express cards
pivot to the bank-linking flow). Absent / `null` = not configured: the SDK falls
back to the host page's client configuration, then its card-only default (bulk off).

Resolution: plain override-fallback: a subaccount value overrides the account value
when set (no master gate). An explicit `bulkEnrollment`
flag in the SDK's `open()` config wins over this policy in SDK v1. In SDK v2 the
server value wins field by field over `open()`; the boolean is read only when
`bulkEnrollment` is absent (`true` is `suggested`, `false` is `off`), and a boolean
`bulkEnrollment` in `open()` is itself read as a set of rails (`true` is card on,
bank `on`, bulk `suggested`; `false` is card on, bank `amex-only`, bulk `off`).

cardEnrollment.description:
Unified-SDK rail: offer manual card enrollment (PAN entry + 3DS verification).
Resolution: live per-field override-fallback (subaccount value if set, else account).

bankEnrollment.description:
Unified-SDK rail: offer bank linking. `on` = offered for every network that can link a bank (a route after the card number in SDK v2, a chooser tile in SDK v1); `amex-only` = reachable only via the American Express card number; `amex-visa` = the American Express route plus the Visa rule below (an interim mode while a program's Visa approval is pending; still reachable only through the card number; expected to be retired once approval lands: do not build long-lived integrations on it); `off` = disabled. Resolution: live per-field override-fallback, except for the two account settings at the end of this description.

Under `amex-visa`, `POST /card-subscriptions` single-enrolls a Visa card only when its BIN is classified as business: a `cardCategory` of `BUSINESS`, `CORPORATE`, `FLEET` or `PURCHASING`, or, when `cardCategory` is absent or `UNKNOWN`, a `type` of `COMMERCIAL`, `CORPORATE` or `SMALL_BUSINESS` (the fields `GET /bin-lookup` returns). It refuses every other Visa card with `403`. Unless another enrollment control refuses the card first, the code is `card_subscription.subaccount_blocking_card_type` and the body adds `reasonCode: card_subscription.bank_enrollment_required` and `cardClass`, the class the rule read (`CONSUMER`, `PREPAID`, `GIFT`, `SPECIALTY`, or `UNCLASSIFIED` when the BIN has no class). A refused credit card can enroll through bank linking (`POST /bank-links`) instead, and the unified SDK sends it there itself; the SDK offers no bank route to a debit or prepaid Visa card. `POST /enrollment-methods` with a `subaccountId` names this refusal `bank-enrollment-required` in `singleDecision.reason`. Bulk enrollment is not affected.

Rollout note for `amex-visa`: SDK bundles released before this value treat it as
`off` (lenient parsing turns an unknown rail value into the safest mode), and
`off` disables bank linking ENTIRELY: a program sitting on `amex-only` that is
flipped early does not merely miss the new Visa pivot, it loses its existing
American Express pivot and Amex cards cannot enroll at all. The SDK deploy must
precede flipping any account or subaccount to this value, and rolling the SDK
bundle back while accounts still carry `amex-visa` re-opens the same hazard in
reverse.

Astrada can lock the account's value: while `bankEnrollmentLocked` is `true`, the
account's `bankEnrollment` applies to every subaccount.

An `amex-visa` set on the account applies to every subaccount too, with or without the lock: subaccount reads return `amex-visa` whatever the subaccount stores. Stored subaccount values are kept.

bankEnrollmentLocked.description:
Astrada-admin lock on the account's `bankEnrollment`. Customers cannot set it: it is
read-only on subaccounts, and `PATCH /subaccounts/{subaccountId}` ignores it.

Set on the account only, together with an account-level `bankEnrollment`. While it is
`true`, the account's `bankEnrollment` applies to every subaccount, whatever value a
subaccount stores. Stored subaccount values are kept and apply again once the lock is
cleared.

Subaccount reads return `bankEnrollmentLocked: true` while the lock is on and omit the
field otherwise. Account reads return the stored value. While the lock is on,
`POST /bank-links` can refuse a link that the account's `bankEnrollment` does not allow,
with `403` and the code `BANK_ENROLLMENT_DISABLED`.

bulkEnrollment.description:
Unified-SDK rail: offer network bulk-feed enrollment for bulk-capable programs.
`suggested` = the bulk flow (the kickoff form in SDK v2, a wizard in SDK v1) offered
next to a connect-this-card-now option; `forced` = the bulk flow
is the only path for bulk-capable cards; `off` = no bulk routing (direct card
form). Supersedes the deprecated `bulkEnrollmentEnabled` boolean; when both are
set, the SDK prefers this field. Resolution: live per-field override-fallback.

bankEnrollmentLocked.description:
Read-only. `true` while the account has locked `bankEnrollment`, and the account's
`bankEnrollment` then applies whatever value the subaccount stores. Absent otherwise.
A subaccount accepts no value for it: the lock is set on the account only.

plaid-end-customer.description:
Admin-managed policy controlling whether an account's bank links are created under the
account's own Plaid reseller End-Customer (EC) client instead of the shared legacy client.
Fields are optional and nullable; absent fields leave the current value unchanged, explicit
`null` clears a field.

enabled.description:
Master gate for routing this account's bank links through its own Plaid reseller
End-Customer client. Absent / `null` / `false` → disabled (legacy shared client).

Admin-set, account-level. When `true`, the account's bank links are created under the
account's own Plaid reseller End-Customer client; once that client is provisioned and
Plaid's registration with the relevant institutions has completed, the hosted Link
experience carries the account's own branding (display name and Link customization)
rather than Astrada's. Enabling an account whose End-Customer client is not yet
provisioned fails link creation rather than silently falling back to the shared client.

Resolution is passthrough from the account onto the effective subaccount read: this
object is account-level only in v1 (there is no subaccount-level override) and
subaccount GETs return the account's stored value as their **effective** value.

bank-linking-policy.description:
Admin-managed policy controlling which account types and institutions are offered when
linking bank accounts via the hosted (Plaid) flow. Fields are optional and nullable;
absent fields leave the current value unchanged, explicit `null` clears a field.

Resolution is per-field and LIVE: a subaccount field applies when set; when absent/`null`
the parent account's value applies; when neither is set the field reads `null` and the
system default is applied downstream at bank-link creation
(`accountTypes: [credit]`: credit-card accounts only, the historical behavior).
Subaccount GETs return these EFFECTIVE resolved values (nulls included; the default is
never materialized in reads).

Bank-link creation uses a copy of the policy read at most 60 seconds earlier, so a change
can take up to a minute to apply. When that read fails, the create uses the system default
for that call.

accountTypes.description:
Account types selectable during bank linking. Enforced by the provider at link-token
creation (Plaid account_filters: checking/savings → depository subtypes, credit →
credit card); institutions offering none of the allowed types are hidden from
institution search. Default: `[credit]`.

pinnedInstitutionId.description:
Provider institution id to pre-select at link creation (e.g. `ins_10` for American
Express). NOTE: Plaid's `institution_id` pre-selection is currently rejected on
production (`INVALID_INSTITUTION`); this field is stored and forwarded only behind a
provider capability flag; until the provider supports it, institution limiting is
achieved with `plaidLinkCustomizationName` plus account-type filtering.

plaidLinkCustomizationName.description:
Name of a Plaid Dashboard Link customization to pin on created link tokens
(institution shortlist, Account Select mode). The customization must already exist for
the account's Plaid client in the Plaid Dashboard. A `POST /bank-links` may name
`amex_only` in `filters.linkCustomizationName`, which then takes this value's place,
and a policy `amex_only` is not applied to a link whose `bin6` does not start with `3`.
If Plaid refuses the name, `POST /bank-links` answers `403`
`PLAID_CUSTOMIZATION_NOT_PROVISIONED`, except for `amex_only`, which is first retried
once with the environment's pinned customization in its place, or with none.

providers.description:
Open-banking provider allowlist for bank-link creation. Unset/`null` = unrestricted:
the client's requested `provider` governs, bounded only by which providers are
enabled on the platform. Set: a `POST /bank-links` requesting a provider outside the
list is rejected with `400`.

The `mastercard` provider is not yet available in every environment. In an environment
without it, a `mastercard` link is refused with `400` `PROVIDER_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_COUNTRY`.

defaultProvider.description:
Provider used when `POST /bank-links` doesn't name one. Unset/`null` = the system
default (`plaid`).

defaultCountryCode.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country used when `POST /bank-links` doesn't name one.
Unset/`null` = the system default (`USA`).

consent-policy.description:
Which consent records `POST /card-subscriptions` accepts for this subaccount. Astrada sets
it, on the account as a default and on the subaccount as an override; there is no route to
change it. The value is the effective one: each field comes from the subaccount when it sets
one, otherwise from the account, except that an account `mode` of `off` turns the mode off
for every subaccount. Absent (never `null`) when neither level sets a field.

A subaccount with no `consentPolicy` behaves as `log` with every channel allowed. Which mode
a new or existing account starts in: [When consent is required](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/direct-api-card-enrollment-integration#when-consent-is-required).

allowedChannels.description: The channels a consent may come from. A consent from any other channel fails with `consent_channel_not_allowed`.

mode.description:
`off` records nothing, `log` records without refusing, `enforce` refuses a missing or
failing consent. What each mode answers: [When consent is required](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/direct-api-card-enrollment-integration#when-consent-is-required).

subaccount.description:
A subaccount. Every representation of this resource (`GET /subaccounts/{subaccountId}`,
`GET /subaccounts`, and the `POST /subaccounts` / `PATCH /subaccounts/{subaccountId}`
responses) reports the same EFFECTIVE read model: `enforceIssuerCountry`,
`enrollmentPolicy`, `bankLinkingPolicy`, `plaidEndCustomer` and `consentPolicy` are resolved
live against the parent account rather than echoed as stored on the subaccount, and
`networkBlockedCards` is resolved live from the platform network configuration. A write
response therefore matches the subaccount you would read back immediately afterwards, and
can surface account-level and platform-level settings the subaccount stores nothing for.

Exception: `enforceIssuerCountry` is omitted from the `GET /subaccounts` list items.

accountId.description: The unique identifier of the account related to this entity.

id.description: The unique identifier of this subaccount entity.

name.description: The name of this subaccount entity.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

verificationPolicy.description:
The subaccount's card verification policy.

- Copied from the account when the subaccount is created; `PATCH` changes it field by field.
- The tier and `sandbox` use only this value (in the sandbox environment, `sandbox` counts as `true` for every subaccount).
- `failedAttemptLockout` falls back to the account's while the subaccount's policy, or its `failedAttemptLockout`, is `null`.

enforceIssuerCountry.description:
Whether card enrollment is restricted to issuer countries within the account's
capabilities. Account-level setting, resolved onto the subaccount at read time;
there is no subaccount-level override, so the subaccount never stores its own
value. Absent on the subaccount list; `false` when the account has not enabled it.

networkBlockedCards.description:
Platform-level enrollment rules resolved from the network configuration at read time.
Applied before the subaccount's own block lists and not configurable per account or
subaccount. Keyed by network (`VISA`, `MASTERCARD`, `AMEX`); a network with no rules is
omitted. A rule matches a card when `cardType` equals the BIN's `type` and
`fundingTypes` contains the BIN's `fundingType`. An omitted or empty `fundingTypes`
matches every funding type. Enrolling a matching card fails with
`card_subscription.network_blocking_card`.

enrollmentPolicy.description:
Enrollment policy. Fields are the EFFECTIVE values: the unified-SDK rails
(`cardEnrollment`, `bankEnrollment`, `bulkEnrollment`) and the deprecated
`bulkEnrollmentEnabled` resolve as subaccount-overrides-account, and are SPARSE; only
explicitly-configured fields appear; `linkAnotherCard` resolves live to `false`
when either level stores an explicit `false` (absent everywhere = enabled, field
omitted). `bankEnrollmentLocked` is read-only: it
appears, as `true`, only while the account has locked `bankEnrollment`, and
`bankEnrollment` is then the account's value. `null` means the subaccount stores
no policy and neither a rail nor `linkAnotherCard` is set at the account level
(account-level admin snapshot fields do not surface through a `null` here).

plaidEndCustomer.description:
Plaid End-Customer routing. `enabled` is the EFFECTIVE value; resolved
from the parent account. This object is account-level only: there is no
subaccount-level override, so the subaccount never stores its own value. `null` means
the account has Plaid End-Customer routing disabled.

bankLinkingPolicy.description:
Admin-managed bank-linking policy. Fields are the EFFECTIVE values;
per-field live resolution against the parent account (subaccount field if set,
else account, else `null`). A whole-`null` policy means neither level has one
set. The credit-only system default (`accountTypes: [credit]`) is applied
downstream at bank-link creation, not materialized in this read.

consentPolicy.description:
The effective consent policy, set by Astrada. A subaccount with no `consentPolicy` behaves
as `log` with every channel allowed, and an account `mode` of `off` turns the mode off for
every subaccount. Which mode a new or existing account starts in: [When consent is required](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/direct-api-card-enrollment-integration#when-consent-is-required).

`SGP`.
