blockedFundingCardTypes.description: Funding card types blocked for Mastercard single enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

blockedCardTypes.description: Card types blocked for Mastercard bulk enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

blockedFundingCardTypes.description: Funding card types blocked for Mastercard bulk enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

amex-countries.description: The American Express country codes (ISO 3166 alpha-3) a subaccount enrolls cards in, each listed once.

amex-countries-or-wildcard.description:
Either an array of ISO 3166 alpha-3 country codes (the contracted regional areas for
American Express), each listed once, or the string `"*"`, which inherits all countries from
the parent account's AMEX capabilities.

Accepted codes: `USA`, `CAN`, `GBR`, `ITA`, `SWE`, `AUS`, `NZL`.

blockedCardTypes.description: Card types blocked for AMEX single enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

blockedFundingCardTypes.description: Funding card types blocked for AMEX single enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

blockedCardTypes.description: Card types blocked for AMEX bulk enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

blockedFundingCardTypes.description: Funding card types blocked for AMEX bulk enrollment. The account's defaults for this network and enrollment mode are always added, so the stored list can include values that were not sent.

create-subaccount-configurations.description:
Subaccount network and regional configurations which determine the available networks and geographies during card enrollment.

The `countries` property for each network accepts either:
- An array of ISO 3166 alpha-3 country codes (e.g. `["USA", "CAN"]`)
- The string `"*"` to inherit all countries from the parent account's capabilities for that network

When `"*"` is used, the subaccount automatically reflects the parent account's current country list. If the parent account's capabilities change, subaccounts using `"*"` will inherit the updated countries. API responses always return the resolved country list, never the `"*"` literal.

The single and bulk enrollment configurations are optional. Countries are set per network: each one's country list is the network's `countries`, limited to the countries the account allows for that way of enrolling. The supported card types for single and bulk enrollment is CONSUMER, while the supported funding card types is DEBIT. If not provided, the block rules for both card types will default to the parent account's default block rule for that network and enrollment level. A list you send is combined with the account's defaults, so it can add blocks but never remove one of the account's defaults. Visa consumer debit and prepaid cards are blocked at the network level regardless of these settings; see `networkBlockedCards` on the subaccount.

Inside `single-enrollment` and `bulk-enrollment`, only `blockedCardTypes` and `blockedFundingCardTypes` are read. Any other key is ignored, not refused: a `countries` there (reads return the countries Astrada works out for each way of enrolling), and a misspelled name too, so a block list sent as `blockedCardType` is not saved and the account's default applies.

The same holds higher up: inside a network only `countries`, `single-enrollment` and `bulk-enrollment` are read, and at the top only `VISA`, `MASTERCARD` and `AMEX`. Any other key there is ignored, not refused. So a network sent as `Visa` is dropped: on create the subaccount is made without it (with no network left, the request is refused with `Configuration is not a subset of the Capabilities.`), and on `PATCH`, if the subaccount has Visa, the request is refused with `Delete a configuration is not supported.` (or with `Configuration is not a subset of the Capabilities.` when no network is left in the body), because every network the subaccount has must be sent.

To set the default rule on the parent account, please reach out to your account manager or support.

customer-enrollment-policy.description:
The customer-writable subset of the enrollment policy: the three unified-SDK
rails. All other fields (`linkAnotherCard`, `bankEnrollmentLocked`, and the
deprecated `bulkEnrollmentEnabled`) are managed on the internal
enrollment-policy endpoints and are ignored if sent here. The `200` names
every ignored key, these and misspelled ones alike, in `ignoredFields`.

Fields are optional and nullable; absent fields leave the current value
unchanged, explicit `null` clears the subaccount-level value. A cleared
rail falls back to the account-level value when one is set; only when
neither level sets the rail does it disappear from reads, letting the
host page's client configuration and then the SDK's card-only default
apply.

cardEnrollment.description:
Whether the unified SDK offers manual card enrollment (PAN entry + 3DS
verification).

bankEnrollment.description:
Whether the unified SDK offers bank linking. In SDK v2 the bank link is a route after the card number, not a separate tile: `on` offers it for every network that can link a bank (SDK v1 shows a chooser tile instead); `amex-only` keeps it reachable only via the American Express card number; `amex-visa` is the American Express route plus a Visa rule: a Visa card enrolls through `POST /card-subscriptions` only when it is classified as business, and the SDK sends every other Visa card to the bank route, except a debit or prepaid one (a temporary mode for programs whose Visa approval is pending: expect it to be retired once approval lands; do not build long-lived integrations on it); `off` disables it (American Express cards then can't enroll unless a bulk program qualifies).

Before setting `amex-visa`, confirm with your Astrada contact that the
SDK release supporting it is live: older SDK bundles treat unknown rail
values as `off`, which disables bank linking entirely, the existing
American Express pivot included.

Astrada can lock the account's `bankEnrollment`: the subaccount's
`enrollmentPolicy` then returns `bankEnrollmentLocked: true`. While it is
locked, the account's value applies. The value you set here is kept, and
has no effect until the lock is removed.

An `amex-visa` set on the account applies to every subaccount in the same way, without a lock: the subaccount's `enrollmentPolicy` returns `amex-visa` whatever value you set here. The value you set is kept, and has no effect while the account's value is `amex-visa`.

bulkEnrollment.description:
Whether the unified SDK offers network bulk-feed enrollment for
bulk-capable programs. In SDK v2 the bulk flow is the kickoff form, reached
from the program screen or the callout after the card number (SDK v1 shows a
bulk wizard). `suggested` offers it next to a connect-this-card-now option;
`forced` makes it the only path for bulk-capable cards; `off` skips bulk
routing entirely (direct card form).

verificationPolicy.description:
Set or clear fields of the subaccount's card verification policy. Fields you send
replace those fields and fields you leave out keep their value; the policy as a
whole cannot be sent as `null`. Customers may set any
level above LOW (MEDIUM, HIGH, HIGHEST), send a null level to clear the
override, toggle the `sandbox` test flag, and set `failedAttemptLockout`.
LOW is internal-only and is rejected on this endpoint.

ignoredFields.description:
The keys of the request's `enrollmentPolicy` that this endpoint
ignored, each written as `enrollmentPolicy.<key>`: every key other than
`cardEnrollment`, `bankEnrollment` and `bulkEnrollment`, such as a
misspelled key or a field Astrada manages. Nothing is stored for them,
and the accepted keys are applied as usual. Absent when no key was
ignored.

id.description: The link's identifier.

url.description: The link to share. Its secret follows `#`, and only this response returns it.

expiresAt.description: After this time no session starts from the link.

maxUses.description: The session starts the link allows.

transaction-embedded.description:
Related resources inlined on request with the `expand` query parameter
(`?expand=cardSubscription,card,cardholder`). A key is present only when it was requested and the
related resource exists, and it is never null. Each embedded body is identical to the one served by
the resource's own endpoint. Absent entirely when `expand` is not sent. Embedded resources show their
current values, not those at the time of the transaction, with one exception: `cardholder.corporate` is
the cardholder's corporate as of the transaction's `transactionOccurrenceDate` (end of that UTC day), or
its `createdAt` when that is null.

`cardSubscription` is the transaction's card subscription exactly as
`GET /card-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` serves it (not itself expanded): the card's subscription in
the transaction's sub-account, that is the one from the transaction's network bulk feed when the
transaction has a `networkBulkFeedId`, otherwise the card's current subscription, otherwise its most
recent one. Fields that apply only to some subscriptions (for example network bulk feed ones) follow
that endpoint's rules.

`card` is the transaction's card (`cardId`) exactly as `GET /cards/{cardId}` serves it (not itself
expanded, so it never carries its own `_embedded.cardholder`). `cardholder` is that card's cardholder as
`GET /cards/{cardId}/cardholder` serves it, except that `corporate` (`id`, `employeeId`,
`alternativeEmployeeId`, `legalEntity`) is the value in effect at the transaction's date while every other
field is current; absent when the card has no cardholder data. When `GET /cards/{cardId}` would respond
`404` for the card (for example because all of its card subscriptions were deleted), neither `card` nor
`cardholder` is present. When `cardId` is null, none of the three keys is present. Presence is decided on
the card and cardholder as they are now.

Transaction webhooks can also carry `_embedded` (see [Event Types](https://docs.astrada.co/reference/event-types)).

transaction-acceptor.description: The details relating to the acceptor (merchant) from the latest transaction message.

city.description: The acceptor's registered city. Defined by the acquirer/processor.

country.description: The acceptor's registered country following ISO 3166 alpha-3.

mcc.description: The Merchant Category Code provided by the acquirer/processor. Used to classify businesses by the types of goods provided or services rendered.

state.description: The acceptor's registered state (e.g. Michigan) as assigned by the acquirer/processor.

cardId.description: The unique identifier of the card related to this entity. Null only for bank-sourced transactions on a bank account with no linked cards (the card-less unified feed); the `_links.card` link is omitted in that case.

cardholderBillingCurrency.description: The currency of the country of issuance following ISO 4217 alpha-3 format.

cardholderBillingHoldAmount.description: This amount models the hold on the cardholder account, in the card's issued currency, that occurs after an authorization and before a financial message. This amount will change as both authorization and financial messages are added to the Transaction in order to reflect the remaining hold amount. A pending refund (an approved credit authorization) reflects its signed amount here as a negative hold while pending, released back to zero once the clearing financial message settles it.

cardholderBillingSettledAmount.description: The settled amount models the bottom line impact to the customer's bank statement in the card's issued currency. This amount will change as financial messages are added to the Transaction.

controlAccountNumber.description: The American Express Basic Control Account number associated with the card, as provided by the Amex real-time authorization (RTA) and General Ledger (GL) feeds. Treat it as an opaque string and keep it exactly as returned: it is numeric today and may contain leading zeros, so never parse it as a number. Present only on American Express transactions where the feed supplies it; absent for all other networks and for transactions ingested before this field was introduced. It is never returned as null or an empty string. This is an account identifier, not a card number.

id.description: The unique identifier of this transaction entity.

network.description: The card network that processed this payment.

networkBulkFeedId.description: The network bulk feed that delivered this transaction's first feed-carrying message (SmartData for Mastercard, VBDS for Visa clearing). Present only on transactions sourced from a network bulk feed; absent otherwise. Transactions delivered before the producers began emitting this field, or never delivered via a bulk feed, omit it entirely. It is never returned as null or an empty string.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

supersededMessageIds.description: Message ids from `_links.messages` whose financial contribution was superseded during aggregation; typically duplicate deliveries of the same clearing across network feeds, or a provisional bank-sourced settlement replaced by the network clearing. Superseded messages stay listed in `_links.messages` for audit but do not count toward the settled amounts, so exclude them when deriving totals from individual messages (or better, use `transactionSettledAmount` / `cardholderBillingSettledAmount` directly). Always a subset of `_links.messages`. Each payload carries the full current set (a snapshot, not a delta). Transactions last updated before this field was introduced report `[]` until their next update.

status.description: A semantic understanding of the state of the transaction within the transaction lifecycle. `VOIDED` is not final: a clearing can still arrive after a full reversal, and the transaction then moves to `SETTLED` at the cleared amount. [Learn More](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/transaction)

transactionCurrency.description: The currency in which the transaction took place following ISO 4217 alpha-3 format.

transactionHoldAmount.description: This amount models the hold on the cardholder account, in the currency the transaction was conducted in, that occurs after an authorization and before a financial message. This amount will change as both authorization and financial messages are added to the Transaction in order to reflect the remaining hold amount. A pending refund (an approved credit authorization) reflects its signed amount here as a negative hold while pending, released back to zero once the clearing financial message settles it.

transactionOccurrenceDate.description: The UTC date when the transaction took place, following ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This is a date-only field with no time component.

transactionSettledAmount.description: The settled amount models the bottom line impact to the customer's bank statement in the currency the transaction was conducted in. This amount will change as financial messages are added to the Transaction.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

transaction-message-acceptor.description: The details relating to the acceptor (merchant) that initiated the transaction message.

acquirerId.description: The identifier of the acquirer/processor used by the acceptor as assigned by the network.

city.description: The acceptor's registered city. Defined by the acquirer/processor.

country.description: The acceptor's registered country following ISO 3166 alpha-3.

id.description: The identifier of the payment acceptor (merchant) as assigned by the acquirer/processor.

mcc.description: The Merchant Category Code provided by the acquirer/processor. Used to classify businesses by the types of goods provided or services rendered.

state.description: The acceptor's registered state (e.g. Michigan) as assigned by the acquirer/processor.

transaction-message-bankData-personalFin.description: Provider categorization of the bank transaction; the one bank-only datum with no card-side equivalent.

transaction-message-bankData.description: Bank-side provenance, present only on bank-sourced messages (null otherwise). Deliberately slim; the bank's merchant string, dates and amounts map into the canonical fields above; `bankTransactionId` is the stable join key back to the bank feed. It equals `banktransaction.created.id` and `transaction.match.created.matches[].id`, and resolves via `GET /bank-transactions/{id}` for the full bank record.

provider.description: Open banking provider that observed the bank transaction. `mastercard-open-finance` appears once the Mastercard rail is enabled for the subaccount; the payload shape is identical across providers.

bankTransactionId.description: The bank transaction entity id; the canonical, lifecycle-stable join key across every bank-data surface.

id.description: The unique identifier of this transaction message entity.

approvalCode.description: Unique code that authorizes a transaction message, sent by the card issuer/issuer-processor when approving a transaction. Always absent on bank-only messages; no card authorization occurred (its absence, together with the `bank_`-prefixed transactionReference, is the marker of a bank-only message).

traceId.description: The American Express trace identifier for this transaction message. Populated only when `network` is `AMEX`, where it is the reconciliation handle used to match against Amex settlement data. Amex real-time authorizations are not observed to carry an `approvalCode`, so `traceId` is the identifier to reconcile on. The value is a numeric string and leading zeros are significant, so treat it as an opaque string and never parse it as a number; its width can vary by Amex feed, so do not assume a fixed length. Null on every other network; Visa and Mastercard authorizations correlate on `transactionReference` / `approvalCode` instead. Treat null as normal, not as an error.

discountAmount.description: The issuer-reported discount that the merchant netted from the settled amount. Today this is populated for Corpay fleet fuel coupons on Mastercard SmartData clearings. It is a positive amount in the message's `cardholderBillingCurrency`. The parent transaction's `cardholderBillingSettledAmount` is grossed up to the pre-discount statement figure, so `discountAmount` is informational. Use it to reconcile the settled amount against the receipt or fuel-card statement, which shows the discounted figure. Null on every other message, including authorizations and clearings with no coupon. Treat null as normal, not as an error.

cardId.description: The unique identifier of the card related to this entity. Null only for bank-sourced messages from a bank account with no linked cards (the card-less unified feed).

cardType.description: The type of card used in the transaction. The only available value is 'virtual' and the field is nullable.

cardholderBillingAmount.description: The amount in the currency of the country of issuance. The transactionAmount and cardholderBillingAmount values may differ in case of international transactions.

cardholderBillingCurrency.description: The currency of the country of issuance following ISO 4217 alpha-3 format.

createdDateTime.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

dateTime.description:
The timestamp of the transaction message (e.g. authorization, movement of funds, etc) following ISO 8601 format. The timezone depends on the card network:
- **Visa/Amex**: UTC (suffixed with `Z`)
- **Mastercard**: Local time zone of the merchant/acquirer (no `Z` suffix, timezone offset not included)

The presence or absence of the `Z` suffix indicates whether the value is UTC or local time.

Some messages carry an end-of-day value rather than the moment they happened:
- **Visa clearings** (`FINL_ADVC`, `FINL_REQU`): the settlement date at `23:59:59Z`.
- **Visa reversals** (`AUTH_ADVC` with a negative `transactionAmount`): `23:59:59Z` on the UTC day Astrada received the reversal.
- **Amex clearings**: the business date at `23:59:59Z`.

For the date of the purchase itself, use the transaction's `transactionOccurrenceDate`.

messageType.description: The type of operation this transaction message represents. [Learn More](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/transaction-message)

network.description: The rail that processed this payment. `OPEN_BANKING` marks a bank-sourced message with no card-network involvement (the concrete provider is in `bankData.provider`).

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount related to this entity.

result.description: The issuer's decision on whether the transaction message is authorized.

transactionAmount.description: The amount of the transaction message in the currency it was charged in. In the case of international transactions, the transactionAmount and cardholderBillingAmount may differ due to being in different currencies.

transactionCurrency.description: The currency in which the transaction took place following ISO 4217 alpha-3 format.

transactionReference.description: Identification of the Transaction that has to be unique for a time period.

transactionType.description: Types provide additional information about the transaction message, describing the effect that it had on the customer account and the type of accounts affected. [Learn More](https://docs.astrada.co/docs/transaction-message)

transmissionDateTime.description: The timestamp of when the transaction message was received by the data source (i.e. Mastercard or Visa), in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

raw.description: The raw payload from the network that originated the underlying transaction message (will vary by network and message).

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

bin-lookup-warning.description: A note about the answer, with a code to branch on.

code.description:
A stable code for programs to branch on. New codes may be added; ignore codes you
don't recognize.

message.description: A human-readable explanation. The wording may change.
message.example: These digits match card ranges in more than one country. Send up to 11 digits of the card number for a precise issuer country.

bin.description:
The 6-digit Bank Identification Number (BIN) the answer was found under. It is always
the first 6 digits of the `bin` you sent, even when you sent more; the rest of your
input is never echoed back.

network.description: The card network (e.g., VISA, MASTERCARD, AMERICAN_EXPRESS). American Express is `AMERICAN_EXPRESS` here; other endpoints spell it `AMEX`.

type.description: The card type (e.g., COMMERCIAL, CORPORATE, CONSUMER, SMALL_BUSINESS )

fundingType.description: The card funding type (e.g., prepaid, debit, credit)

cardCategory.description:
The card's commercial classification, carried through from the BIN reference dataset.
More specific than `type`: it separates `FLEET`, `PURCHASING` and `GIFT` cards that
`type` reports as `COMMERCIAL` or `CORPORATE`, and it is populated for many BINs where
`type` is absent. `UNKNOWN` means the reference data does not classify the BIN; treat
it as "not determined", not as "consumer".

cardFundingType.description:
How the card is funded, carried through from the BIN reference dataset. Broader than
`fundingType`: it separates `CHARGE` cards (which `fundingType` reports as `CREDIT`)
and `GIFT` cards (which `fundingType` reports as `PREPAID` or `DEBIT`). `UNKNOWN` means
the reference data does not classify the BIN.

issuerName.description:
The name of the issuing bank. For a Mastercard card, this can be more specific to the
digits sent than the 6-digit BIN's issuer name (see `issuerCountry`).

issuerCountry.description:
The country of the issuing bank following ISO 3166 alpha-3. May be `null` when the
BIN is known but the reference data does not record its issuing country (an unknown
BIN returns 404, not `null`).

For a Mastercard card, this is checked against the digits sent and can differ from what
the first 6 digits alone would give, because one BIN can be shared by issuers in several
countries. Send more digits (up to 11) for a more precise issuer country; never send the
full card number.

issuerCountryAmbiguous.description:
Present, and always `true`, only when the digits sent match card ranges in more than
one country. `issuerCountry` is then the 6-digit BIN's value and may not be this card's
country; `issuerCountryCandidates` lists the possible countries and `warnings` explains
what to do. With fewer than 11 digits, sending more can resolve it. Omitted in every
other case.

issuerCountryCandidates.description:
The possible issuer countries (ISO 3166 alpha-3, sorted, at least two) when the digits
sent match card ranges in more than one country. Present only together with
`issuerCountryAmbiguous: true`.

issuerRegion.description:
The region of the issuing bank, derived from the issuer country. `EU` covers Europe
and `MEA` covers the Middle East & Africa. These are separate buckets; there is no
combined `EMEA` value. `UNKNOWN` means the issuer country is missing or not mapped
to a region; treat it as "not determined". It always matches the returned
`issuerCountry`.

warnings.description:
Notes about the answer that a caller may want to act on. Present only when there is
something to report, and never empty. Branch on `code`; `message` is for people and
may change.

Today the only code is `ISSUER_COUNTRY_NOT_CONFIRMED`, sent together with
`issuerCountryAmbiguous: true` when the digits sent match card ranges in more than one
country. With fewer than 11 digits, sending more digits (up to 11) may confirm the
issuer country. With 11 digits, the issuer country could not be confirmed.

bin-lookup-validation-problem-item.description: One problem found in a BIN lookup request.

instance.description: The part of the request the problem is about.

bankAccounts.description: Links to the bank accounts created from this link. Only present when state is `completed` and accounts exist.

bank-link-lastRejection.description: Present while `state` is `pending` after a completion attempt was refused because the connected institution is not allowed for this link (for example, a non-Amex institution on an Amex-restricted link). The link can still be completed by reconnecting with an allowed institution; a successful completion clears this field.

institutionName.description: Display name of the refused institution.

at.description: When the refusal happened, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

bank-link-lastMintFailure.description: Present once a completion attempt was aborted because card creation (the `bank-feed` mint) failed for one or more discovered credit accounts. The link stays pending and completion is retried; a later successful completion clears this field (an expired link keeps its last failure). `transient` failures resolve on retry; a `permanent` one keeps aborting until investigated.

at.description: When the failed completion attempt happened, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

kind.description: Whether the underlying failure is expected to clear on retry.

failedAccountCount.description: How many discovered credit accounts failed to mint on the attempt.

bank-link-filters.description: The account filtering actually applied to this link, after resolution against the account's bank-linking policy. Echoes what the hosted session will offer; absent on links created before filtering existed.

accountTypes.description: Account types selectable in the hosted session.

linkCustomizationName.description: The Plaid Link customization this link asked for: the request's `filters.linkCustomizationName`, or else the bank-linking policy's `plaidLinkCustomizationName`. Absent when neither applies. When Plaid refused `amex_only` and the create was retried without it, this still reads `amex_only`, and the link's completion is still held to American Express institutions.

bank-feed-card.description: A card created from a bank account at bank-link completion (a `bank-feed` enrollment), with its subscription.

id.description: The minted card's identifier on the cards platform.

subscriptionId.description: The bank-feed card subscription created by the mint.

last4digits.description: The card number's last 4; equals this account's mask by construction.

network.description: The card network when the institution implies it (e.g. `amex`); null until a PAN enrollment upgrades the card in place.

enrollmentType.description: Always `bank-feed`; the enrollment transport this card was materialized through.

bank-link-bank-account.description: A bank account created from a bank link, in summary.

id.description: The bank account identifier.

name.description: The display name of the bank account.

institutionName.description: Display name of the connected institution. Present on this API response; not included on the `banklink.completed` event payload.

mask.description: Last 4 digits of the account number. For `credit` accounts this is the card number's last 4; the per-card identity for bank-connected (e.g. American Express) enrollments. Not guaranteed per-card when the institution combines multiple cards into one account.

cardIds.description: Identifiers of already-enrolled cards linked to this account, matched when an enrolled card's last 4 equals a credit account's mask (applied at completion and by a scheduled sweep that re-checks each cardless credit account every few hours). A link is an association to an EXISTING card, not a new enrollment.

cards.description: Cards created from this account at completion (`bank-feed` enrollments), each paired with its subscription. Present only on credit accounts that created a card; a created card also appears in `cardIds`.

noLinkReason.description:
Why this credit account has no card. Present on this API response; not included on the `banklink.completed` event payload. Present ONLY while the account is still cardless; once any card links, the field disappears.

A credit account can legitimately finish linking with no card, and this says which case it was rather than leaving an unexplained empty `cardIds`:
  - `bulk_card_owns_mask`: a bulk-enrolled card is the live owner of this last 4. It correctly suppresses a duplicate card, and a bulk subscription cannot take an automatic bank-account link.
  - `mask_ambiguous_accounts`: several accounts on this link share the mask, so no automatic link is safe.
  - `mask_ambiguous_cards`: several enrolled cards share the mask, and card-number (BIN) evidence could not narrow them to one.
  - `card_linked_elsewhere`: the matching card is already linked to another bank account.
  - `card_not_attachable`: the matching card has no active subscription to attach to.
  - `no_institution_id`: the provider reported no institution, so no stable card identity can be derived.
  - `mask_matches_no_plausible_card`: enrolled cards share the mask, but BIN evidence ruled every one of them out for the connected institution (wrong issuing bank, or debit/prepaid funding), so nothing linked rather than linking a known-wrong card.

The scheduled mask sweep and a manual `PATCH cardIds` both remain available; the field describes the state at completion, not a permanent verdict.

id.description: The client-provided identifier of the bank link. Must be alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores only.

accountId.description: The unique identifier of the account that owns this bank link.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount associated with this bank link.

state.description:
Current state of the bank link.
- `pending`: The link has been created and is awaiting user enrollment.
- `completed`: The user has successfully connected their bank account.
- `expired`: The link has expired without being completed.

provider.description: Open-banking provider this link was created on. Fixed at creation: every later operation on the link uses this value. Links created before provider selection existed are `plaid`.

hostedLink.description: The hosted URL where the user can complete the bank enrollment. This link expires after 4 hours and is automatically refreshed when retrieved via GET.

linkExpiresAt.description: Date and time when the hosted link expires, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

completedAt.description: Date and time when the bank link enrollment was completed, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format. Only present when state is `completed`.

bankAccounts.description: Summary of bank accounts created from this link. Only present when state is `completed` and accounts exist.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

cursor.description: Cursor to use for the next page of results.

hasMore.description: Whether there are more results available.

banking-error.description:
The error body of the Banking API: plain JSON with `statusCode` and `message`. The card APIs use a different body (`title` and `detail`). Branch on `code` where a refusal carries one; `message` is text for people.

One exception: a `401` for a missing or invalid token comes from the gateway, before the request reaches the Banking API, and carries `title` and `detail` like the card APIs.

statusCode.description: The HTTP status code of the answer, repeated in the body.

message.description: What went wrong, in words. Some messages carry ids or states, so do not parse it.
message.example: Subaccount not found for this account

code.description: A stable name for the refusal, such as `SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`. Present on some refusals only.

error.description: The name of the HTTP status, such as `Not Found`. Present on some refusals only.

reason.description: Why the refusal happened, on the refusals that name one. For example, `BANK_ENROLLMENT_DISABLED` carries `network-not-allowed` when the account's setting does not allow a bank link for that card network.

errors.description: The validation problems, on a `400` for a request that did not pass validation. Each item has a `path`, the place of the field in the request; its other fields come from the validation library and can change.

bank-link-create-params-filters.description: Optional per-link narrowing of the account's bank-linking policy. Values may only NARROW what the policy allows; the current system default is `accountTypes: [credit]` (credit-card accounts only). Requests widening beyond the policy are rejected with `400`. Account-type enforcement is applied by the provider at link-token creation and also filters the institution-select list.

accountTypes.description: Account types selectable during this hosted session.

linkCustomizationName.description:
Name of an allowlisted provider (Plaid) Link customization to apply to this hosted session, such as `amex_only` to surface an Amex-first institution list with a tailored headline for card-enrollment connections. Only `amex_only` is accepted; any other name is rejected with `400` (`INVALID_LINK_FILTERS`). A requested customization takes the place of the bank-linking policy's. Institution steering is by account-type filtering plus the customization's Dashboard configuration; the provider does not support hard institution pre-selection for hosted sessions.

With `amex_only` the link completes only at American Express: a sign-in at another institution leaves the link `pending` with `lastRejection`. Send `bin6` with it only when it starts with `3`: a link with another `bin6` is refused at American Express and cannot complete.

bank-link-consent.description: The bank-link consent record. The Unified Enrollment SDK sets it on channel `sdk-unified`, naming the Astrada consent text of the bank-connect screen the person saw. Integrators do not send it. Astrada relays it to each card subscription the bank link creates, where it is recorded and never refused. A consent without `textVersionId` is accepted but not kept.

textVersionId.description: The id of the bank-connect consent text the SDK showed, such as `sdk-unified:bank-consent.plaid.bank.en@v1`.

textHash.description: `sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the text named by `textVersionId`, compared with the registered text when sent.

sdkVersion.description: The SDK release that collected the consent.

variables.description: `companyName` and `providerName`, as the screen showed them. For a Plaid link, Astrada adds `plaidLinkSessionId` when it relays the record.

id.description: A client-provided identifier for the bank link. Must be alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores only.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount identifier to associate with this bank link. A subaccount that does not belong to the account is rejected with `404` (`SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`).

bin6.description: First 6 digits captured client-side before an institution pivot (e.g. an American Express BIN typed into the card form before the SDK pivots to bank linking). Persisted with the link. Attached as the completion-time bank-derived card's `first6digits` when the completion has exactly one eligible candidate account.

provider.description: Open-banking provider to create the link on. Omitted, the subaccount's configured default applies (system default: `plaid`). A provider outside the subaccount's configured allowlist, or one not enabled on the platform, is rejected with `400`. The provider is fixed at creation: every later operation on the link uses the value it was created with.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country of the institution to connect (e.g. `USA`, `DEU`). Omitted, the subaccount's configured default applies (system default: `USA`). Combined with `provider` to select the concrete integration; a country the selected provider does not support is rejected with `400`.

language.description: Language of the hosted bank-linking screens, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en`, `en-US` or `fr-CA`. A tag that matches the pattern is accepted; any other value is rejected with `400`. For a Plaid link, the language part of the tag (`fr` for `fr-CA`) is used when Plaid supports it, Astrada has turned that language on, and no Link customization applies to the link (one it asks for, one from the bank-linking policy, or one Astrada sets for the environment). Otherwise the screens are in English and the request still succeeds. Plaid Link supports `da`, `nl`, `en`, `et`, `fr`, `de`, `hi`, `it`, `lv`, `lt`, `no`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `es`, `sv` and `vi`. Plaid's Norwegian is `no`, so `nb` and `nb-NO` fall back to English. Other providers ignore this field. The language is kept with the link, so a refreshed hosted link uses it again.

persona.description:
Who the bank login belongs to. `cardholder`: a page for one person, such as an employee, who links their own bank login. `admin`: the company. Omitted, the link is a company link, as with `admin`, which is how every link behaved before this field existed.

The link's owner decides which cards its accounts can join: two bank accounts can count as the same card only when their links have the same owner. Cardholder links sent with the same `cardholderKey` share an owner, a cardholder link without a key is its own owner, and every company link has the company as its owner, so a cardholder link never joins a company link's card.

cardholderKey.description:
Your stable id for the person on the page, used only with `persona: cardholder`, so that all of their links share one owner. Optional: without it, each cardholder link is its own owner. A key sent with `persona: admin`, or with no `persona`, is ignored. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and 1 to 256 characters must remain. Astrada stores only a keyed hash of the key, never the key itself.

The key must be one that no other user can guess: an opaque value your backend issues for that person and gives only to their page, such as a random id, or an HMAC of their employee id made with your own secret. Never send an email address, an employee number or anything else another user could guess. A guessed key can join another person's card.

state.description: The target state for the bank link. Only `completed` is accepted.

webhooks.description: The events this sync sends. Default (field left out) is both. An empty array sends neither; transactions are still stored and matched. Names outside this list are ignored, not refused.

force.description:
Set to `true` to force a full sync even if no new transactions are detected. With `true`:

- Stored transactions: every transaction already stored for the link is gone over again, and `banktransaction.created` is sent again for each when `webhooks` allows it.
- Existing matches: scored again, and `transaction.match.created` sent again, only when `webhooks` lists `transaction.match.created`. With `webhooks` left out they are kept and not sent again.
- Unmatched transactions: whatever `webhooks` lists, a stored transaction with no match yet goes through matching, and a new match is sent when `webhooks` allows it.

id.description: The unique identifier of the bank account.

accountId.description: The unique identifier of the account that owns this bank account.

subaccountId.description: The unique identifier of the subaccount associated with this bank account.

bankLinkId.description: The identifier of the bank link that created this account. Null for accounts that predate persisted link attribution.

externalId.description: The provider account ID for the connected account.

cardIds.description: The identifiers of cards linked to this bank account for transaction matching, always current. A card links when its last 4 digits match this account's mask (the same rule applied at bank-link completion and by a scheduled sweep that re-checks each cardless credit account every few hours), or when set manually via PATCH. Cards must belong to the same subaccount.

noLinkReason.description: Why this credit account has no card. Present ONLY while the account is still cardless; once any card links, the field disappears, so it can never contradict `cardIds`. See the identically-named field on the bank link response for the full meaning of each value.

cards.description: Cards MATERIALIZED from this bank account (`bank-feed` enrollments minted at bank-link completion for credit accounts whose mask matched no already-enrolled card). Distinct from `cardIds`, which is the link surface: a mask-matched card appears in `cardIds` only, while a minted card appears in both. Empty for depository and mask-matched-only accounts.

institutionName.description: The name of the connected financial institution.

institutionId.description: The provider identifier of the connected institution (Plaid `ins_*`). Null for connections made before this field was captured.

name.description: The display name of the bank account (e.g. "Checking", "Savings").

mask.description: The last 4 digits of the account number. For `credit` accounts this is the card number's last 4; the per-card identity for bank-connected (e.g. American Express) card enrollments. Not guaranteed to be per-card when the institution combines multiple cards into a single account.

type.description: The normalized type of bank account. (Correction: the service has always returned normalized values; the previous `depository`/`credit` enum understated live behavior. Codegen consumers should regenerate.)

subtype.description: The raw provider account subtype (e.g. Plaid `credit card`, `checking`). Null when the provider did not supply one or for accounts connected before this field was captured.

currency.description: The currency of the account following ISO 4217 format.

state.description:
Current state of the bank account.
- `active`: The account is connected and functioning normally.
- `auth_required`: The account requires re-authentication.
- `disconnected`: The account has been disconnected from the provider.

subscriptionState.description: The health of the underlying aggregator connection backing this account. The account `state` above can read `active` while the connection has errored or needs re-auth, so this field can read "active but dead". Null if no subscription is linked.

lastSyncedAt.description: Last successful sync of the backing connection, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format. Pairs with `subscriptionState` as the freshness signal. Null until the first sync.

createdAt.description: Date and time when this resource was created, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when this resource was last updated, in UTC, following ISO 8601 format.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount whose enrolled cards and bank accounts to match.

linked.description: bankAccountId -> cardIds linked in THIS run.

subaccountId.description: The subaccount to run maintenance over.

mint.description: After the mask pass, also mint a bank-feed card for each of the subaccount's eligible credit bank accounts that holds no card. Accounts that already hold a minted card are skipped.

backfillJunctionLast4.description: After the mask pass, also fill each of the subaccount's card links with the last 4 it answers to, where still unknown, from the cards directory.

createCardholderCards.description: After the mask pass, also create and name the bank-feed cards of the cardholders behind the subaccount's pooled American Express billing accounts, as the scheduled job does. Does nothing unless Astrada has switched the feature on for the subaccount.

bank-account-maintenance-result-junction.description: Present only when `backfillJunctionLast4: true` was sent.

rowsUpdated.description: Links that gained a last 4 in this run.

rowsUnresolved.description: Links still without one (the directory did not list the card).

directoryUnavailable.description: True when this action's own read of the cards directory failed (the mask pass does not fail on it); call again later.

bank-account-maintenance-result-cardhold.description: Present only when `createCardholderCards: true` was sent. Counts only; no cardholder name is ever returned.

enabled.description: False when card creation is not switched on for the subaccount; nothing was created.

routeEnabled.description: True when each cardholder's transactions are emitted on their own card.

accounts.description: Pooled American Express billing accounts served.

suffixesSeen.description: Distinct cardholders (by the card's last 4) seen in those accounts' transactions.

created.description: Cardholder cards created in this run.

linkedEnrolled.description: Cards the cardholder had already enrolled, linked instead of creating one.

named.description: Cards whose cardholder name was written in this run.

relinked.description: Cardholder cards found on another bank account of the subaccount after a re-link, left where they are and counted (the background re-home moves them).

failed.description: Cards that could not be created this run; the next run tries again.

skipped.description: Reason -> count of cardholders given no card of their own (their transactions stay on the account's main card). Reasons: `no_primary`, `ambiguous_primary`, `bulk_owned`, `ambiguous_enrolled`, and the permanent `deactivated`, `not_active`, `unlinked` and `foreign_reuse`. Only reasons with a count appear.

directoryUnavailable.description: True when this action's own read of the cards directory failed; no card was created this run.

linked.description: bankAccountId -> cardIds linked in THIS run.

minted.description: Present whenever `mint: true` was sent (`{}` when nothing was minted). bankAccountId -> the card minted for it in THIS run. `linkedHere` is false when the card is held by a sibling account instead (a re-link of the same bank; the background re-home converges it).

skipped.description: Present whenever `mint: true` was sent (`{}` when nothing was skipped). bankAccountId -> why the mint pass did not mint for it: `already_materialized` (the account already holds a minted card), `existing_enrolled_card` (its last 4 belongs to a card the customer enrolled directly) or `no_institution_id` (the connection never recorded its institution).

failures.description: Present whenever `mint: true` was sent (`{}` when no mint failed). bankAccountId -> the failure. The pass is idempotent, so the request can simply be repeated.

bank-account-cards-update-backfill.description: Optional backfill configuration to import historical bank transactions for the linked card.

startDate.description: Start date for the backfill range in YYYY-MM-DD format.

endDate.description: End date for the backfill range in YYYY-MM-DD format.

cardIds.description: The identifiers of cards to link to this bank account for transaction matching. Send an empty array to unlink all cards. Each card must belong to the same subaccount.

state.description: Set to `disconnected` to stop this account's feed and remove its card links while keeping the account, its transactions and its matches readable. With `cardId`, see that field: the account can keep feeding its other cards. This endpoint cannot set it back: a new bank link to the same bank creates a new bank account, and this one stays `disconnected`. When this is the connection's last active account, the connection at the bank is ended too. Disconnecting an account that is already disconnected, or one that was deleted, answers `200` and sends no webhook (an id that never existed still answers `404`). Use `DELETE /bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}` to remove the account and its transactions.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason recorded with the disconnect. Sent as `reason` on `bankaccount.state_changed`. Default `subscription_deactivated`.

cardId.description: Optional SCOPE for the disconnect. Omit for the historical account-scoped behaviour: the whole account is torn down and every card on it loses the feed. Supply the card that was deactivated to scope it to that card: its link is removed and the account keeps feeding any other cards attached to it. Disconnecting the last remaining card still tears the account down, so a single-card account behaves identically either way.

bank-account-update-result-backfill.description: The result of the backfill, when the request asked for one and added at least one card. If fetching history from the bank data provider fails, matching still runs on the bank transactions already stored, and this object is returned with counts for those. It is left out when a later step fails (reading the stored or card transactions, or matching); the update itself still stands. The fields mean the same as on `POST /bank-accounts/{bankAccountId}/backfill`, except that matching here only looks for the cards this request added.

transactionsProcessed.description: Unmatched bank transactions in the window that matching looked at, whether imported by this call or already stored.

matchesFound.description: Matches found against the cards this request added.

cardId.description: The card whose card transaction this bank transaction is matched to. Stamped when a match is persisted and cleared if a later forced rematch supersedes that match, so it is only ever non-null alongside `matchId`. Null while unmatched, including on accounts with linked cards: linking alone never attributes individual bank transactions.

matchId.description: The identifier of the transaction match, if this bank transaction has been matched to a card transaction.

currency.description: The currency of the transaction following ISO 4217 format.

transactionType.description:
The type of transaction.
- `debit`: Money sent (outflow).
- `credit`: Money received (inflow).

source.description:
The source of this transaction.
- `PLAID`: Synced from a connected financial institution via Plaid.
- `UPLOAD`: Imported from a manually uploaded bank statement.
- `MASTERCARD_US`: Synced from a connected financial institution via Mastercard Open Finance US. Sandbox only.
- `MASTERCARD_EU`: Synced from a connected financial institution via Mastercard Open Finance Europe. Sandbox only.

status.description:
The lifecycle stage of the bank movement, derived from its match pointer and settlement state.
- `posted`: Synced, not yet matched.
- `matched`: Paired to a card transaction without an early settlement of its own (e.g. connector off, or a below-HIGH match): the movement is represented by the card transaction's network settlement, and any standalone it previously emitted is netted to zero.
- `settled`: A bank-only movement settled standalone on the unified feed.
- `early_cleared`: A matched movement settled its card transaction early.
- `superseded`: A previously bank-only movement was retracted or corrected.

ids.description: List of bank transaction identifiers to emit webhooks for. Must contain at least one ID.

webhooks.description: The types of webhook events to emit. Leave it out and only `banktransaction.created` is sent.

forceRematch.description: Set to `true` to re-run the matching algorithm for the named transactions before emitting webhooks. Transactions that already have a match are genuinely re-scored: the existing match id is preserved when the pairing survives, updated when a better pairing exists, and removed when the movement no longer matches.

Requires `forceRematch: true` and `webhooks` to include `transaction.match.created`; the request is rejected with `400` otherwise, because only a same-run re-match can distinguish a genuinely unmatched movement from a duplicate of an already-settled purchase.

against any network. When omitted, the scenario's own default

scenario emits, so simulated activity can be attributed to a

The transactions created by the scenario. Each entry lists the
ids of the transaction messages published for that transaction;
use `GET /transaction-messages/{transactionMessageId}` to
retrieve each message once it has been processed.

simulate-transaction-request-merchant.description:
The merchant (card acceptor) on the message. Defaults to a fixed sandbox
coffee-shop merchant in the United States.

name.description: Merchant name, emitted as the transaction descriptor.

country.description:
Merchant country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (for example `USA`,
`GBR`, `FRA`), case insensitive; any other value is rejected with
`400`. Defaults to `USA`.

simulate-transaction-request.description:
Starts a new simulated transaction on an enrolled sandbox card by publishing
a single transaction message. Every field other than `cardId` and `type` is
optional and falls back to a default.

cardId.description:
The identifier of the enrolled card to transact against. The card must
belong to the account of the access token; the subaccount and, unless
`network` is given, the network are read from the card.

type.description:
The first message of the new transaction.
- `authorization`: publishes an authorization request, creating a
  `PENDING` transaction with `amount` on hold.
- `settlement`: publishes a clearing with no prior authorization,
  creating a `SETTLED` transaction with `amount` settled and nothing on
  hold. A later `authorization` step on the transaction joins it.

amount.description:
Transaction amount in minor units of `currency` (for example `4500` for
45.00 USD). Defaults to `4500`.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the transaction, case
insensitive. Must be a currency transactions can be made in; fund codes
and precious metals are rejected with `400`. Defaults to `USD`.

network.description:
Card network the message is published on. Defaults to the card's own
network; the request is rejected with `400` when this field is omitted
and the card has no network or one outside this list.

dateTime.description:
Timestamp of the message, ISO 8601 with a timezone offset. Must not be in
the future. Defaults to the time of the request.

messageId.description:
The id of the transaction message that was published. Once it has been
processed, use `GET /transaction-messages/{transactionMessageId}` to
retrieve it, or `GET /transactions?transactionMessageId=` to find the
transaction it created or updated.

simulate-transaction-message-request.description:
Publishes one more transaction message on an existing sandbox transaction.
The message reuses the transaction's card, network, currency, merchant and
network reference, so the new message joins the same transaction.

type.description:
The message to publish. `amount` is in minor units of the transaction's
currency; whether it is required depends on the type:
- `authorization`: an additional authorization that increases the hold.
  `amount` is required.
- `adjustment`: replaces the current hold with `amount` (the new total).
  `amount` is required. Rejected with `409` when nothing is on hold.
- `reversal`: releases `amount` from the hold. Defaults to the full
  remaining hold. Rejected with `409` when nothing is on hold or when
  `amount` exceeds the hold.
- `settlement`: clears `amount`, moving it from the hold to the settled
  amount. Defaults to the remaining hold; required when nothing is on
  hold.
- `refund`: negative settlement linked to this transaction. Nets into it
  while it is still PENDING or on accounts that correlate refunds;
  otherwise (the default for API-created accounts) a SETTLED transaction
  gets a separate refund transaction with its own `transaction.created`.
  Defaults to the settled amount; required when nothing has been settled.

amount.description:
Amount in minor units of the transaction's currency. See `type` for
which types require it and what it defaults to otherwise.

dateTime.description:
Timestamp of the message, ISO 8601 with a timezone offset. Must not be in
the future. Defaults to one second after the transaction's latest
message, or to the time of the request if that is later; when the latest
message is already ahead of the clock (an end-of-day message, see below),
the time of the request. Set an earlier value to backdate a message (for
example an authorization that joins a settlement-first transaction).

As in production, Visa settlements and reversals and Amex settlements
are published with an end-of-day `dateTime`: the UTC date of this value
at `23:59:59Z`.

networkReference.description:
- Gl: The Amex Recipient ID for the bulk feed, in the format
'R{RecipientId}', such as 'R12345', or the 6-digit Company ID the
feed was created with. Must match the feed created via
`POST /network-bulk-feeds`.
- Smartdata: The Mastercard Delivery ID for the bulk feed, such as 'G1234567'.
Must match the feed created via `POST /network-bulk-feeds`.
- Vbds: The Visa RPIC identifier for the bulk feed, made of the Visa region,
processor, issuer and company segments joined by '_'
('{region}_{processor}_{issuer}_{company}'), such as
'1_12345_67890_54321'. Must match the feed created via
`POST /network-bulk-feeds`.
- Vcf: The Visa reference for the bulk feed. Pass the same value used
to create the feed via `POST /network-bulk-feeds`: the full
RPIC '{region}_{processor}_{issuer}_{company}', such as
'1_123_45_6789'; the region segment is ignored. The 3-segment
PIC form '{processor}_{issuer}_{company}' is also accepted.

cardCount.description:
- Gl: Number of cards to include. For an `encrypted` feed these are
drawn from the head of the sandbox account pool: the same
accounts every call; once enrolled in the subaccount they
deduplicate. For a `tokenized` feed they are drawn from the
enrollable 374290-BIN Amex token pool (two tokens). Requesting more than the
tokenized pool holds does not error: the call still returns
`202` and under-delivers (only the enrollable tokens are
written), so do not build a retry on an expected `400`. When
omitted, defaults to 3 for encrypted feeds and to the whole
enrollable token pool for tokenized feeds. When `cardCount` is
sent, `cardCount + newCardCount` must be at least 1.
- Smartdata: Number of cards from the head of the sandbox test-card pool to
include. These are the same cards every call; once enrolled in
the subaccount they deduplicate. `cardCount + newCardCount`
must be at least 1.
- Vbds: Number of cards from the head of the sandbox card pool to
include. These are the same cards every call; once enrolled
in the subaccount they deduplicate. `cardCount + newCardCount`
must be at least 1.
- Vcf: Number of cards from the head of the sandbox test-card pool to
include. These are the same cards every call; once enrolled in
the subaccount they deduplicate. `cardCount + newCardCount`
must be at least 1.

While a feed has not completed an ingestion (normally its
first call), a call with `newCardCount` of `0` also adds one
card the feed's subaccount has not seen before, so the feed
can become active.

newCardCount.description:
- Gl: Number of not-yet-enrolled accounts to draw from the sandbox
pool for this feed's subaccount. Each call enrolls this many
new cards (with `cardsubscription.created` webhooks). Requires
an active feed for the `networkReference`; returns `400` when
none exists or when the subaccount has exhausted the pool. Not
supported on `tokenized` feeds: a value greater than 0 on a
tokenized feed returns `400` (there is no tokenized new-card
pool).
- Smartdata: Number of not-yet-enrolled cards to draw from the sandbox
new-card pool for this feed's subaccount. Each call enrolls
this many new cards (with `cardsubscription.created`
webhooks). Requires an active feed for the `networkReference`;
returns `400` when none exists or when the subaccount has
exhausted the pool.
- Vbds: Number of not-yet-enrolled cards to draw from the sandbox
pool for this feed's subaccount. Each call enrolls this many
new cards (with `cardsubscription.created` webhooks). Requires
an active feed for the `networkReference`; returns `400` when
none exists or when the subaccount has exhausted the pool.
- Vcf: Number of not-yet-enrolled cards to draw from the sandbox
new-card pool for this feed's subaccount. Each call enrolls
this many new cards (with `cardsubscription.created`
webhooks). Requires an active feed for the `networkReference`;
returns `400` when none exists or when the subaccount has
exhausted the pool.

transactionsPerCard.description:
- Gl: Number of settlements generated for every included card
(written as a companion settlement file), with fresh
transaction ids and recent dates on each call. Use `0` for a
cards-only file.
- Smartdata: Number of transactions generated for every included card, with
fresh transaction references and recent dates on each call.
Use `0` for a cards-only (starter) file.
- Vbds: Number of settlements generated for every included card, with
fresh transaction ids and recent dates on each call. Use `0`
for a cards-only delivery.
- Vcf: Number of transactions generated for every included card, with
fresh transaction references and recent dates on each call.
Use `0` for a cards-only (starter) file.
